## Highlights
* (macOS) **DirectX graphics support for Windows**: Modern accelerated graphics for Windows 11 is now available on UTM for the first time. The driver is still experimental and games compatibility is currently limited.
* **Vulkan 1.3 graphics support for Linux**: Vulkan 1.3 is now supported on Linux guests with VirtIO Venus drivers in Mesa. Additionally, OpenGL 4.1 is supported with the new Apple Core OpenGL backend (macOS only).
* **Snapshots**: Save your VM at any point and go back to it later from the new Snapshots tab. Works with QEMU VMs on macOS and iOS 26, and with Apple Virtualization VMs on macOS 27.
* (macOS) **Apple Virtualization on macOS 27**: Pass USB devices through to your VM, turn on Secure Boot for Linux, run a VM without saving changes, and let VMs talk to each other with new networking modes.
* (macOS) **Smoother displays**: VMs now follow your display's refresh rate, so motion is fluid at up to 120 Hz on ProMotion displays.
* **More reliable USB**: Fast external SSDs can now be shared with a VM, and disconnecting a drive no longer freezes UTM. On macOS, drives are safely unmounted before they are handed to a VM.
* (iOS) **Better touch controls**: Gestures respond immediately, with new middle-click and right-drag actions and a new drag-to-scroll touch mode.
* (iOS) **iPhone Duo**: Fold your iPhone Duo like a laptop, and the bottom half becomes a keyboard or touchpad for your VM.

## Notes
* Suspended VMs may not resume correctly after updating. We recommend shutting down all VMs before you update UTM.
* The minimum supported versions are now macOS 12 and iOS 15.
* (macOS) Check out [UTM Games Database](https://db.getutm.app/) to see and report game compatibility for the experimental 3D driver. Re-install the Windows guest tools to get the latest driver.
* We now have a [development blog](https://blog.getutm.app)! Follow us for in-depth technical deep dives such as how we brought DirectX to QEMU.
* (macOS) To use the new graphics driver for Windows 11, we recommend a fresh install because the driver is still experimental and its use could lead to instability in the system. During the install of the guest tools, you will be prompted to select the experimental graphics driver. If you wish to install the new driver on a system that already is running the older display only driver, you need to run the uninstall script provided on the guest tools install ISO first.
* (macOS) Apple CoreGL backend does not support Vulkan or DirectX.
* Linux desktop rendering in Vulkan does not work due to lack of support for indirect draws for geometry shaders. Please configure your guest to use the older VirGL Gallium driver.
* SCSI drives on ARM64 virtual machines now use a VirtIO SCSI controller. A VM with a SCSI drive that was suspended, or has a snapshot with saved state, from an earlier version cannot resume it: delete the saved state and start the VM again.

## Changes (v5.0.9)
* (macOS 14) Display: Reverted the fix for VM windows being limited to 60 fps on ProMotion displays, because it could crash a VM at startup (#8204) and blurred Retina mode (#8191). VM windows still run at 120 Hz on a ProMotion display, unless a slower external display is the main display (added 2026-11-18)
* Fixed Windows games hanging at startup while compiling shaders, in-game videos stalling after the first frame, and a failed 3D command resetting the guest's display (#7984)
* Fixed X11 apps under Xwayland not displaying with Vulkan on Linux
* Updated the virglrenderer, MoltenVK and DXMT graphics backends
* Security: Fixed memory corruption issues that could allow a malicious guest to gain sandboxed code execution in the isolated rendering process (thanks Xusheng Li at Vector 35 Inc)
* Home: VM notes now render Markdown (#3547) (thanks @pingu-the-penguin)
* Home: Fixed the confirmation for Clone, Stop or Move not appearing the second time it was requested for the same VM (thanks @ianplusplus)
* Home: Fixed the screenshot in the VM details being covered by a flat color on iOS 26, macOS 26 and visionOS 26
* Home: The size shown in the VM details now updates after the settings are closed (#7923)
* Home: A VM on an external drive that is listed as unavailable now stays available after its .utm is opened again (#7762)
* Home: Fixed one unreadable saved entry making every VM lose its saved location, window state and external drives
* Config: SCSI drives on ARM64 virtual machines now use a VirtIO SCSI controller, so guests without an LSI driver such as Rocky Linux and RHEL can see them (#7712)
* Config: Fixed PowerPC VMs created with the default settings failing to start because of too many CPU cores
* Config: Fixed the default devices of the Heathrow PowerMac (g3beige) machine keeping the VM from starting (#7803)
* Config: Fixed the default configuration of the Sam460ex machine failing to start (#7603)
* Config: Fixed new PowerPC VMs such as pseries defaulting to a network card that the machine rejects (#7592)
* Config: Fixed saving a VM failing after adding a TPM on RISC-V and LoongArch
* Config: Fixed a crash opening the terminal window of a VM whose configuration has no terminal settings
* Config: Fixed the host port of port forwards being replaced by the guest port when migrating a UTM 3 configuration
* QEMU: Guests with a VirtIO GPU now use the host display's refresh rate instead of always 75 Hz (#7820) (thanks @dragoshont)
* QEMU: Fixed saving a VM state that takes longer than 10 seconds being reported as "Timed out waiting for RPC" (#8052)
* QEMU: Fixed networking and the guest agent stalling once QEMU holds about a thousand open files, such as with a busy shared directory or 3D acceleration (#7624)
* QEMU: Fixed the display modes missing from the Monitors control panel of Mac OS guests on the mac99 machine (thanks @giovariot)
* QEMU: Fixed sound in Mac OS 9 and a hang at startup in its sound driver (#8033)
* QEMU: Fixed Mac OS 9 restarting to a black screen (#7999)
* QEMU: Fixed sound crackling

## 29.10.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.10.0 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.10.0)
- [moby/moby, 29.10.0 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.10.0)

### ⚠️ Potential breaking change: local registry connections

If you explicitly configure `insecure-registries` in `daemon.json` or use `--insecure-registry`, Docker Engine no longer automatically treats loopback addresses (`127.0.0.0/8` and `::1/128`) as insecure registries.

> [!WARNING]
> After upgrading, pulls and pushes to local registries that use HTTP or untrusted TLS certificates may fail unless those registries are explicitly included in your insecure registry configuration.
> Configure TLS with a trusted certificate, or add only the required local registry addresses, such as `localhost:5000`, to your existing insecure registry configuration.

When `insecure-registries` is omitted, loopback registries remain insecure by default.
Setting `"insecure-registries": []` in `daemon.json` disables all default insecure registries. [moby/moby#53868](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53868)

### 🧻 Engine API specification moves to OpenAPI 3.2

The Engine API specification now uses OpenAPI 3.2 as its source format, in [`api/openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/api/v1.57.0/api/openapi.yaml).
A Swagger 2.0 specification generated from it is still published for existing tooling, in [`api/swagger.yaml`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/api/v1.57.0/api/swagger.yaml).
For the transition, this release also includes a Swagger 2.0 copy pinned to API v1.57, in [`api/docs/v1.57-swagger.yaml`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/api/v1.57.0/api/docs/v1.57-swagger.yaml).
Future API versions won't get a per-version Swagger 2.0 copy, so update tooling that depends on these files to use the OpenAPI 3.2 specifications. [moby/moby#53630](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53630)

### 📦 Packages for AlmaLinux, Oracle Linux, and Rocky Linux

Docker Engine packages are available for AlmaLinux, Oracle Linux, and Rocky Linux.
For installation instructions, see [AlmaLinux](/manuals/engine/install/almalinux.md), [Oracle Linux](/manuals/engine/install/oraclelinux.md), and [Rocky Linux](/manuals/engine/install/rockylinux.md).

---

### New

- Add experimental support for jobs: run one-shot and cron-scheduled workloads natively managed by the daemon, as an opt-in built-in extension enabled with `--enable-extension org.mobyproject.jobs.v0`. [moby/moby#53485](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53485)
- Add support for customizing Docker’s embedded containerd using configuration files in `/etc/docker/containerd.d/`. [moby/moby#53946](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53946)
- Introduce `restarting` attribute for  `die` events to let consumer know container is going to restart. [moby/moby#50908](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/50908)

### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Block obsolete socket families in the default AppArmor and seccomp profiles. [moby/moby#54093](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54093)
- containerd image store: Fix `docker image inspect` and `docker image ls` reporting an empty image when the host platform of a multi-platform image is not pulled but another platform is. [moby/moby#54040](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54040)
- Don't wait for the telemetry export timeout when the OTLP endpoint refuses connections. [docker/cli#7495](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7495)
- Fix `docker <unknown-command> --version` printing the CLI version instead of an "unknown command" error. [docker/cli#7408](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7408)
- Fix `docker cp` printing a "Successfully copied" message when the copy fails. [docker/cli#7515](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7515)
- Fix `docker manifest annotate` rejecting valid platforms not included in its predefined list of OS/architecture combinations, such as `linux/loong64`. [docker/cli#7448](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7448)
- Fix `docker ps` printing an empty `NAMES` column when all of a container's names contain a slash, such as when connected to a classic Swarm API. [docker/cli#7481](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7481)
- Fix the daemon deleting the docker0 interface on restart when it is configured with a user-managed bridge and default-address-pools. [moby/moby#54157](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54157)
- Fix Windows layer exports containing NTFS sparse files. [moby/moby#53745](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53745)
- Fix: Include HTTP status codes in JSON streaming errors to allow clients to correctly classify failures. [moby/moby#54133](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54133)
- Improve image selection on ARM64 Linux hosts to prefer the highest image variant supported by the host CPU. [moby/moby#53910](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53910)
- manifest annotate: add shell-completion for `--os` and `--arch`. [docker/cli#7449](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7449)
- Reject duplicate GPU counts consistently when shorthand and explicit count options are mixed. [docker/cli#7312](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7312)
- Stop automatically treating loopback registries as insecure when `insecure-registries` is explicitly configured, and allow disabling the default insecure registries by setting `"insecure-registries": []` in `daemon.json`. [moby/moby#53868](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53868)
- Update runc (in static binaries) to [v1.5.3](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases/tag/v1.5.3). [moby/moby#54183](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54183)

### Packaging updates

- Update BuildKit to [v0.35.0](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.35.0). [moby/moby#54180](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54180)
- Update Go runtime to [1.27.4](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.27.4). [moby/moby#54176](https://github.com/moby

```console
    --certificate-github-workflow-repository cri-o/packaging \
    --certificate-github-workflow-ref refs/heads/main \
    --bundle cri-o.amd64.v1.37.4.tar.gz.bundle
```

To verify the bill of materials (SBOM) in [SPDX](https://spdx.org) format using the [bom](https://sigs.k8s.io/bom) tool (v0.8.0 or later), run:

### New images

- **Odroid C5** | Support and images for this new Hardkernel SBC with Amlogic S905X5M SoC have been added.
- **Orange Pi 6/6 Plus** | Support and images for these new Orange Pi 6 family SBCs with CIX P1 dodeca-core (12) SoC have been added. The image uses a generic ACPI kernel, and bootloader + device tree come from the onboard UEFI firmware. Hence it should work on any CIX P1 board with UEFI and ACPI-capable firmware.
- **Orange Pi Zero 4** | Support and images for this new SBC with Allwinner A733 SoC have been added. It is very similar to the Orange Pi Zero 3W, but adds Gigabit Ethernet. Like for the Zero 3W, Xunlong's Linux 6.6 and U-Boot vendor sources are used.
- **Orange Pi 4A** | Images for this SBC with Allwinner T527 SoC  have been added. Note that it uses a mainline Linux based kernel, which lacks support for CPU scheduling, hence all cores run at a fixed 768 MHz. A patch is in review: <https://lwn.net/Articles/1096895/>

### New software

- **Paperless-ngx** | This document management system turns your scanned paper documents into a searchable online archive, with OCR, automatic tagging and full-text search. It has been added to our software catalogue with ID `paperlessngx`. It is available for ARMv8 and x86_64 systems with at least 2 GiB total memory (RAM + swap). Many thanks to everyone who requested this: <https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/discussions/5489>
- **Yuvomi** | This self-hosted family planner with calendar, tasks, meal planning, shopping lists and budget has been added to our software catalogue. Many thanks to @miloit for implementing this software option: <https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/pull/8461>
- **SolidPing** | This self-hosted uptime monitoring tool with status pages and alerting has been added to our software catalogue with ID `solidping`. Many thanks to @fclairamb for implementing this software option: <https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/pull/8366>
- **Podman** | This daemonless container engine with Docker-compatible CLI and API has been added to our software catalogue with ID `podman`. Like Docker, containers and images are stored in `/mnt/dietpi_userdata/podman-data`, and logs go to the systemd journal. Containers are meant to be run as individual systemd units, e.g. via Quadlet: <https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/pull/8480>

### Removed software

- **Readarr** | It has been archived by its maintainers last year. Use e.g. LazyLibrarian instead. The update won't remove Readarr from your system, so you can keep using it if installed already. Once you found a replacement, see here how to cleanly remove Readarr: <https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/pull/8388>
- **Mono** | This .NET runtime has been superseded by modern .NET since years. It was only needed our end to support running several Servarr applications on ARMv6 Raspberry Pi models, since .NET does not support that architecture. However, those Servarr applications dropped support for Mono years ago, too, hence we needed to install outdated versions on those RPi models, which from at least security perspective is irresponsible. Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, and Jackett has hence been disabled for ARMv6, along with the Mono removal. The DietPi update won't remove software from your DietPi system. We strongly recommend to find an alternative setup. Find instructions about a clean removal of Mono, and in case those Servarr applications on ARMv6, here: <https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/pull/8388>

### New tools

- **dietpi-fan_control** | This new script allows to configure temperature-controlled cooling fans on Raspberry Pi. It can be started via `dietpi-fan_control` command, or from `dietpi-config` > "Performance Options" > "Fan Control". Fans attached to the GPIO header can be driven via hardware PWM (`pwm-fan` overlay, Debian Trixie and later, not on RPi 5), software PWM (`pwm-gpio-fan` overlay), or simple on/off switching (`gpio-fan` overlay). On RPi 5, the trip points of the dedicated PWM fan port can be configured as well. For each trip point, temperature, hysteresis and fan speed can be adjusted. Settings are stored in `/boot/firmware/config-fan.txt`, which is included by `config.txt`, so that fan control can be disabled without losing the trip point settings. Many thanks to @zumbiepig for implementing the new `pwm-gpio` overlay into the official RPi kernel, and starting the implementation of this feature for DietPi: <https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/pull/8269>

### Enhancements

- **Quartz64** | A Linux headers package has been added, which allows to compile kernel modules. Install it via `apt install linux-headers-quartz64`, which works on Model A, B, and SOQuartz the same way. Many thanks to @yoshibox for doing this suggestion: <https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/issues/8470>
- **Odroid C2** | Overlays to enable the HiFi Shield 2/Plus have been added to our kernel builds. The `dietpi-config` audio option entries make use of them, hence have been fixed for mainline Linux.
- **bash** | When completing a word with the `<tab>` key while the cursor is inside it, the characters after the cursor are no longer duplicated if they match the completion. E.g. if `foobarbaz` is a completion option, `foo<cursor>bar<tab>` now gives `foobarbaz` instead of `foobarbazbar`. This change comes along with a bash-completion extension for `dietpi-software` (see below).
- **dietpi-banner** | On Raspberry Pi systems, a warning is now shown if the firmware detected undervoltage or high temperature and in case lowered the CPU frequency and/or voltage in turn. Many thanks to @Marzal for implementing this: <https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi/pull/8203>
- `dietpi-banner` | The pre-login banner with DietPi version, time, date and LAN IP address is now shown by the login prompt itself, on every local, serial and container console, instead of being printed once at the end of the boot process to the main console only. Features:
  * The new authentication policy action `remember_device_idle_timeout` ends the recognition of a remembered device
    that nobody used for the given time, for example `7d`. `remember_device_validity` also accepts a unit, for example
    `8h` or `90m` (#6155)
  * Administrators can list and revoke the remembered devices of a user on the user details page of the WebUI and with
    the new endpoint `GET /clients/remembered_devices`. The new admin policy actions `remembered_device_list` and
    `remembered_device_revoke` give these rights (#6155)
  * The passkey registration requests the WebAuthn extension `prf`, which lets a client application derive a secret
    from the passkey. The new enrollment policy `passkey_disable_prf` turns the request off. The token info of a
    passkey shows details of its registration, for example `attestation_format` and `user_verified` (#6342)
  * The new enrollment policies `applspec.length` and `applspec.contents` set the length and the characters of the
    password that the server generates for an `applspec` token. The request parameters of the same names have no
    effect, as for `pw` and `registration` tokens (#5828)
  * Each token of a container template has the new option "Change PIN on first use". The option also applies if a user
    creates the container or enrolls it via multichallenge. Without the option, the policy `change_pin_on_first_use`
    decides (#6319)
  * The Docker deployment in `deploy/docker/` runs privacyIDEA with a bundled MariaDB or with an external PostgreSQL,
    MariaDB, MySQL or Oracle database. `make init` creates the configuration files, and `make upgrade` makes a backup
    before it starts a new image (#6083, #6329)
  * WebUI: If the user policy `password_reset` is set, the login page offers "Reset Password". The user gets a recovery
    email and sets the new password on a page of the WebUI (#6093)
  * WebUI: Users with the user policy `updateuser` can edit their own user data on their user details page. With
    `set_custom_user_attributes` and `delete_custom_user_attributes`, they can also change their custom attributes
    (#6108)
  * WebUI: The token details and the token enrollment can create a new container, and the user details page adds
    selected tokens to an existing container. The container list filters by template and compares the containers with
    their templates. `GET /container/` accepts the new parameter `has_template` (#6238)

    confirmation of a push token. "Trigger Challenge" needs the admin right `triggerchallenge` (#6291)

    unsaved changes, and the stored policy does not change (#6038)

    notifications. The default level "AA" uses darker colors than 3.14.0, so that white text has a contrast of at
    least 4.5:1 (#6052)

Since the beta of AdGuard Home v1.0 was released in late September, we collected feedback and acted accordingly. The product has gone through major overhaul both under the hood and appearance-wise in the beta versions. The stable release adds the fine-tuning that users asked for. Today, we are releasing AdGuard Home v1.0.

## A redesign you don’t have to relearn

The web interface for AdGuard Home has been completely updated to look cleaner, more modern, and fully aligned with the rest of the AdGuard ecosystem. Avoiding overall layout changes was intentional — we didn’t wish for you to stress out while relearning where every button is. We refreshed the visual style while preserving the familiar logic. We wrote extensively about it in our [article on the beta version](https://adguard-dns.io/en/blog/adguard-home-v1-0-beta.html), it is worth a look if you need more information. 

![New dashboard](https://cdn.adtidy.org/content/release_notes/dns/home-v1-0-beta/dashboard.png)

But this overhaul goes deeper than looks. The new frontend shares the backend’s strict optimization philosophy. Rebuilt with fine-grained reactivity, it is now significantly lighter and faster. This update also resolves memory consumption issues linked to the old interface, making AdGuard Home run smoothly on low-power devices, and introduces a fully responsive mobile UI.

![Before and after](https://cdn.adtidy.org/content/release_notes/dns/home-v1-0-beta/adguard_home_before_after.png)

## New release model

We are adopting a more flexible development and versioning model used by other AdGuard products. Minor releases may now include backward-incompatible changes, which lets us ship features faster.

What does this mean for you? Moving forward, the new release cycle will focus on delivering features and tools, not just patches and library updates.

No migration needed: v1.0 keeps the same configuration schema as v0.107.x, , so your existing configuration works as is.

## What changed since the beta

While the first beta of v1.0 introduced a globally changed interface, the second beta was all about stability. 18 changes were included in it, we will highlight the most important ones below; you can consult the full list in the [changelog](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdGuardHome/releases/tag/v1.0.0-b.2).

* **DHCP:** IPv4 settings can now be saved alongside an IPv6-compatible interface, DHCP starts with a DHCPv6-only configuration, and subnet validation works as expected.
* **Clients and ClientIDs:** IPv6 CIDRs with an embedded IPv4 address are accepted, malformed MAC addresses and leading-zero octets are rejected, and per-client schedules survive saving.
* **Interface:** long values no longer overflow dialogs, encrypted DNS addresses appear in the Setup Guide right away, and emoji passwords work in the wizard.
* **DNS:** DDR returns a valid SVCB record with empty DoH routes, schedules no longer shift on clock changes, and command-line updates work with private reverse DNS enabled.
* **Everything else:** `--check-config` behaves correctly on first launch, and `log.enabled: false` now disables the legacy logger.

One change deserves a special mention. New installations now use *Cloudflare DNS* as the default upstream and bootstrap servers instead of *Quad9*. 

The new defaults are `https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query` for the upstream and `1.1.1.1`, `1.0.0.1`, `2606:4700:4700::1111`, `2606:4700:4700::1001` for the bootstrap. Previously we used `https://dns10.quad9.net/dns-query` with `9.9.9.10`, `149.112.112.10`, `2620:fe::10`, `2620:fe::fe:10`. Existing configurations are not migrated automatically. 

> Users whose traffic goes through France, should update the upstream and bootstrap addresses before November 24, when *Quad9* stops serving the country.

Also, client settings are now more specified: *Use global settings* covers *Protection* only, blocked services have their own switch, and upstream and cache settings stay editable. You can apply global settings when you want many clients to share the same configuration, or set things up per-client when you want an individual approach.

## Our plans for future releases

AdGuard Home v1.0 won’t be the last version to bring major changes — we plan to keep improving it until it reaches its full potential. A self-diagnostics page, mass-importing of filtering lists, a built-in search tool for the interface and the ability to automatically issue and renew TLS certificates are currently in the works. We intend to move the product forward at a faster pace from now on.

## How to update or switch to v1.0

**If you are using the beta or edge channel:** You don’t need to do anything. The update will go through automatically via the built-in updater.

**If you are on the stable version:** Follow the UI prompt to update.

**If you prefer using CLI:** Run the command `./AdGuardHome --update -v`

**If you are updating through Docker:** Set the image tag to `:latest`, then recreate and restart the container.

## DNSSEC security fixes

Thanks to @kevinpark1217 for reporting these seven findings, fixing them, and contributing regression tests. If you use Blocky’s built-in validator (`dnssec.validate: true`), upgrade to v0.37.0. Six fixes affect earlier releases; the seventh hardens code introduced during development of v0.37.0.

- **Chain of trust (GHSA-rfc7-q64c-hj2f):** DS and DNSKEY records must belong to the zone being validated. If Blocky cannot complete validation beneath a trust anchor, it returns SERVFAIL rather than serving unchecked data.
- **Complete answers (GHSA-8mfq-h5hh-mqf2):** Blocky checks that the answer matches the question and response code. A signed alias leading to unsigned data no longer marks the whole answer as authenticated (AD).
- **Authority for negative answers (GHSA-6fgw-qmpq-vwxp):** Proof that a name or record does not exist must come from the zone responsible for it. A signature from another zone is not sufficient.
- **Wildcard and denial proofs (GHSA-mv8x-2h8p-g3wh):** Blocky now requires complete proofs for wildcard answers, nonexistent names (NXDOMAIN), and missing record types (NODATA), including checking for aliases where required.
- **NSEC3 Opt-Out (GHSA-583r-m4vv-q43p):** Blocky requires a complete proof from the parent before treating a delegation as unsigned.
- **RSA signature failures (GHSA-g35c-mff8-4w2w):** A failed signature under a supported algorithm is rejected rather than treated as evidence that the data is unsigned.
- **Validation work limits (development builds only; GHSA-vgm3-vqcv-4hv6):** Blocky bounds RSA exponent size and signature-verification work per query. No prior release shipped the large-exponent fallback affected by this finding.

Apache APISIX 3.21.0 upgrades APISIX Runtime to 1.4.3, protects credentials in forwarded requests and logs, and improves upstream recovery and log delivery.

## Runtime and security fixes

APISIX Runtime 1.4.3 uses the NGINX 1.31.9 core in its OpenResty 1.31.8.1 build. It incorporates ten upstream security fixes. Their relevance to a deployment depends on the enabled modules and configuration. [Runtime upgrade #14223](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14223) · [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

| Component | CVEs |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP/2 | CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633 |
| HTTP/3 | CVE-2026-121810 |
| TLS request bodies | CVE-2026-118899 |
| DNS resolution | CVE-2026-123634 |
| Stream TLS and PROXY protocol | CVE-2026-123640, CVE-2026-120967, CVE-2026-120993 |
| Static file handling | CVE-2026-125283 |
| Mail proxy (disabled in the standard Runtime build) | CVE-2026-113425 |

## Gateway and plugin changes

- With `normalize_uri_like_servlet` enabled, upstream requests now use the query arguments left by rewrite and access plugins. This preserves credential removal by `key-auth` and `jwt-auth`. Mirrored requests honor explicit upstream URI overrides, and `data-mask` applies query masking rules to `upstream_uri` in access logs. [#14163](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14163)
- APISIX stops logging sensitive configuration values during etcd validation and plugin execution. Admin API errors for invalid plugin configuration types report the type without echoing the submitted value. [#14157](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14157)
- Recovered round-robin nodes restart their slow-start ramp. New health checkers observe health transitions during initialization, and Redis cluster probes reuse TLS and authentication settings when checking for recovery. [#14188](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14188) · [#14215](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14215) · [#14181](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14181)
- Logger batch processors preserve active batches during cleanup and correct backlog counts after failures or filtering. The Elasticsearch logger isolates batches by plugin configuration so each Route uses its own endpoints and credentials. TCP and Splunk loggers also improve error handling. [#14192](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14192) · [#14004](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14004) · [#14012](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14012)
- Prometheus includes the first session's bytes in `apisix_stream_bandwidth` for a new service. The host-based router includes the referring Route ID when it cannot load a Service. [#14101](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14101) · [#13723](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/13723)

## Before upgrading from 3.20.0

- **Admin API keys.** When `admin_key_required` is enabled, set an explicit `admin` or `viewer` role on every configured key and quote numeric-looking keys in YAML. Check traditional and control-plane configurations, including traditional deployments with the Admin API disabled. [#14203](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14203)
- **Encrypted configuration.** Newly encrypted plugin configuration and metadata values carry a `$ENC$v1$` prefix. Back up etcd before upgrading and avoid Admin API writes during a rolling upgrade. If encrypted resources have been re-saved, restore the pre-upgrade data before rolling back to the official 3.20.0 source release or another build without marker support. [#14162](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14162)
- **HTTP parsing and source installs.** The new NGINX core rejects header lines missing a colon, returning 400 for client requests or 502 for upstream responses. It also rejects chunked request bodies with excessive framing overhead. When installing from the source archive, install APISIX Runtime 1.4.3 separately, then run `make deps APISIX_RUNTIME=1.4.3`. [#14223](https://github.com/apache/apisix/pull/14223)

## v0.21.12 - 2026-11-17

### Fixed
- Fix Dockerfile `COPY` reading the whole image and keeping a hash record of it in engine memory by @sipsma in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/15040 \
  A plain `COPY` is now keyed on its parent, its arguments and the content of its sources,
  as BuildKit does, and a `COPY --from` of a single file no longer records the source stage's
  whole filesystem. Engines running many Dockerfile builds no longer grow until OOM-killed.
- Fix gracefully stopped services being force-killed when a binding detaches during shutdown by @sipsma in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/15069 \
  A detach of a service that is already stopping is now a no-op, and a graceful stop joins one
  already in flight instead of sending another SIGTERM followed by a SIGKILL 10s later.
- Fix execs escaping the engine pod's CPU and memory limits under Kubernetes by @sipsma in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/15096 \
  The engine now runs in its own cgroup namespace rooted at its container's cgroup, so execs
  nest under the pod's limits as they do under Docker. An exec that exceeds the memory limit
  is OOM-killed on its own and the engine keeps running.
- Fix setting `GitRepository` and `GitRef` arguments from `.env` user defaults by @marcosnils in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/15155 \
  These failed with `Address has no such field: "gitrepository"` while the same value passed
  as a flag worked.

This release contains performance improvements, bug and security fixes since the 2.32.0 release. We recommend that you upgrade at the next available opportunity.

This release is compatible with the latest PostgreSQL minor releases, 18.7, 17.12 and 16.16 ([announcement](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-187-1712-1616-1520-1425-and-19-rc-2-released-3442/)) and above, and is fully backward compatible with older Postgres minor versions. Previous TimescaleDB patch versions are affected by a background worker issue on these newer PostgreSQL minor releases: every job run by the scheduler fails. We strongly recommend that, before upgrading PostgreSQL, you first upgrade TimescaleDB to this version.

**Bugfixes**
* [#10971](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/10971), [#11086](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/11086) Keep the wait after a job crash when the scheduler reloads jobs
* [#11015](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/11015) Fix background jobs failing on new PostgreSQL minor releases
* [#11019](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/11019) Fix internal error when a job commits inside run_job
* [#11028](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/11028) Create chunk indexes without switching to the catalog owner
* [#11029](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/11029) Analyze expressions of columns added to continuous aggregates as the calling user
* [#11031](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/11031) Create indexes on continuous aggregates as the calling user
* [#11032](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/11032) Add foreign keys to chunks as the chunk owner
* [#11035](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/11035) Do not switch to catalog owner for constraint drops and view updates
* [#11037](https://github.com/timescale/timescaledb/pull/11037) Only switch to catalog owner to create tables in the internal schema

Valkey 9.2.0 GA  -  Released Wed 18 November 2026
-------------------------------------------------

Upgrade urgency LOW: This is the first stable release of Valkey 9.2.

### Behavior Changes
* `ZRANGEBYSCORE`, `ZREVRANGEBYSCORE`, `ZCOUNT`, and `ZRANGESTORE` now reject a bare `(` or an empty string as a score bound instead of silently treating it as 0 by @AlisinaDevelo (#4054)
* Path Hash deletion commands now remove the key when the last path is deleted, following the Hash key lifecycle and emitting a generic del event by @yangbodong22011 (#5068)
* Active expiration of keys and hash fields now increments the dirty counter, so save points (and thus BGSAVE) may trigger more often by @enjoy-binbin (#3118)

### New Features and Enhanced Behavior
* Add new `DELEX` command to conditionally delete a string key when its value matches (`IFEQ`) or differs from (`IFNE`) a given value by @lightsigma96 (#4607)
* Add Zstd as a streaming compression codec for RDB persistence and replication, offering better compression ratios than LZ4 by @sarthakaggarwal97 (#3798)
* Support streaming-compressed RDB preambles in AOF bases, so compressed full-sync RDB files can be reused directly as AOF bases by @sarthakaggarwal97 (#4754)
* `ACL GENPASS` and the hash function seed draw randomness from the configured OpenSSL 3 provider when built with TLS, supporting deployments that require a validated crypto module by @MarkAtwood (#4339)
* Support forkless full synchronization to replicas, serving disk and diskless full syncs from a background-thread snapshot without forking by @nitaicaro (#4797)
* Add ACL DIGEST command that returns a fingerprint of the ACL rules currently in effect, useful to verify what ACL LOAD applied by @melancholictheory (#4446)
* Add forkless RDB snapshots, opt-in via the new `forkless-infrastructure-enabled` and `bgsave-default-method` configs, with new INFO persistence fields reporting the save method and progress by @JimB123 (#4460)
* Add the `XACKDEL` and `XDELEX` stream commands with `KEEPREF`, `DELREF` and `ACKED` modes to acknowledge and delete messages once consumer groups no longer need them by @nickiaq (#4629)
* Support a secondary server certificate via `tls-alt-cert-file`, `tls-alt-key-file` and `tls-alt-key-file-pass`, e.g. a post-quantum certificate alongside RSA, with matching INFO TLS fields by @pkhartsk (#3717)
* Add ACL roles: named, reusable sets of ACL selectors managed with `ACL SETROLE`/`DELROLE`/`GETROLE`/`ROLES` and assigned to users with `role:<name>`, in commands, the ACL file and valkey.conf by @yang-z-o (#3967)
* Add a `maxmemory-scripts` config to limit memory used by cached `EVAL` scripts, and mark `SCRIPT LOAD` as DENYOOM so it respects the global maxmemory limit by @enjoy-binbin (#866)
* Add Path Hash, a new radix-tree-backed data type with `PH*` commands for exact lookup, longest-prefix matching, and prefix traversal over binary-safe paths by @yangbodong22011 (#4506)
* Support whole-stream LZ4 compression of RDB files via the new `rdbcompression lz4` option; the default per-string LZF behavior is unchanged by @sarthakaggarwal97 (#3531)
* Add server-side hot key detection with new `HOTKEYS GET`/`RESET` commands, enabled by setting `hotkeys-top-k` by @alon-arenberg (#3708)
* Add optional replication throttling (`repl-throttling-enabled`) that slows client writes when a replica falls behind, avoiding disconnects and full syncs by @harrylin98 (#4356)
* Prioritize system-critical events (cluster heartbeats, replication, slot migration) over heavy client traffic, tunable via the new `priority-preemptive-poll-interval-us` config by @satheeshaGowda (#4076)
* Reserve connection slots for administrative clients: connections from the CIDR ranges listed in the new `priority-subnets` config are tagged as prioritized, `maxclients-reserved` caps normal clients at `maxclients` minus that many slots, and `INFO clients` reports `connected_priority_clients` by @satheeshaGowda (#4005)
* Add `INCREX` command to atomically increment a key by an integer or float while setting its expiration, with `NX`/`XX` conditions by @GavinDmello (#3253)

### Performance and Efficiency Improvements
* Fix long stalls in `SRANDMEMBER`, `ZRANDMEMBER`, `HRANDFIELD` and `SPOP` on a small key whose hashtable is still shrinking from a much larger size by @madolson (#5170)
* Stop treating `LINDEX`, `LRANGE` and `LPOS` as format-changing commands during forkless background iteration, so list reads no longer get write-style handling by @JimB123 (#5283)
* Keep the forkless save queue growing under write load by not counting keys expedited by writes as leftover work by @taham0 (#5298)
* Make BCAST client tracking cost scale with the prefixes a key matches instead of all registered prefixes, so many unmatched prefixes no longer slow writes and the event loop by @madolson (#5183)
* Reclaim memory from sorted sets that shrink or have frequent score updates by compacting sparse B+tree leaves on delete by @rainsupreme (#4526)
* Speed up sorted set score updates in listpack encoding by replacing the score in place when the member keeps its position by @charsyam (#3491)
* Fix quadratic slowdown in `HRANDFIELD` and `SRANDMEMBER` with counts on collections whose elements differ only in letter case by @madolson (#5167)
* Bound the time spent per cycle evicting keys from the client tracking table, avoiding long stalls after lowering `tracking-table-max-keys` by @tanmayBeginsJourney (#4775)
* Speed up the `INFO` command by around 5% by pre-allocating the output buffer by @charsyam (#3413)
* Reclaim client-side caching tracking table entries left by disconnected clients, fixing a memory leak under read-heavy workloads, and include the tracking table in active defrag by @rayjinghaolei (#4190)
* Speed up `ZPOPMIN` and `ZPOPMAX` on B+tree encoded sorted sets by detaching edge items without a key search or copy by @charsyam (#4852)
* Counting a hash's fields with expirations is now O(1) for hashtable-encoded hashes by tracking

## Important features, changes, and deprecations

This section contains important information about new and existing features.

### Java

Support for Java 21 has been dropped. You must upgrade to Java 25.

### DDL statements for the catalog (experimental)

Druid now supports CREATE and ALTER statements to manage metadata in the catalog. Use them to declare a table's columns, time partitioning, clustering, aggregate projections, and physical layout, instead of setting these in each ingestion spec.

This feature is off by default. To enable it, set `druid.sql.planner.enableCatalogDdl` to `true`.

For more information, see [Catalog](https://druid.apache.org/docs/39.0.0/development/extensions-core/catalog).

[#19830](https://github.com/apache/druid/pull/19830) [#20377](https://github.com/apache/druid/pull/20377) [#20452](https://github.com/apache/druid/pull/20452) [#19770](https://github.com/apache/druid/pull/19770) [#19711](https://github.com/apache/druid/pull/19711)

### Kafka header-based filtering

Kafka supervisors can now filter records by their headers. This reduces ingestion CPU and memory use when you only need some of a topic's records.

To use the filter, add `headerBasedFilterConfig` to the supervisor's `ioConfig`. Use an `in` filter where `dimension` is the header name and `values` lists the header values to ingest. Records whose header value isn't in the list are dropped, and offsets still advance.

Filtering is permissive: records are ingested if they don't have the header, if the header value is null, empty, or can't be decoded, or if evaluation fails.

The new `ingest/events/filtered` metric reports how many records header filtering dropped.

[#18525](https://github.com/apache/druid/pull/18525)

### Typed query context parameters

Common query context parameters listed in [Query context reference](https://druid.apache.org/docs/39.0.0/querying/query-context-reference) and [Scan queries](https://druid.apache.org/docs/39.0.0/querying/scan-query) are now typed `QueryContextParameter` descriptors. The following changes apply to the query context handling:

* Integer and long parameters reject values that aren't exact integers instead of truncating or wrapping them. For example `1.5`, and values out of range. Integral values like 5.0 or "5.0" are still accepted. Invalid values now fail with an error message: "Query context parameter [x] should be ...."
* A null in the query context, or SET x = NULL, no longer clears a default configured with `druid.query.default.context` or the Broker dynamic configuration. The default applies as if the key were not set. Previously the null reached readers, which used the built-in default. To override a configured default, set an explicit value.
* `maxSubqueryBytes` is a typed string parameter that accepts auto, disabled or a non-negative number of bytes, as the subquery guardrail does. Invalid values such as `SET maxSubqueryBytes = TRUE` now fail during validation, and numbers such as `1e9` are now accepted.

[#20555](https://github.com/apache/druid/pull/20555/)

### Druid JDBC driver

Druid now provides its own JDBC driver that uses the `/druid/v2/sql/` endpoint. We recommend that you switch from the Avatica driver to this driver. The new driver provides the following benefits: driver-side connection management that doesn't require sticky load balancing, streaming results, support for SET statements, and support for non-native SQL engines.

[#19951](https://github.com/apache/druid/pull/19951)

### Netty 4.2

Druid now uses Netty 4.2 for its HTTP client. Previously, Druid used Netty 3. This is a substantive change in memory characteristics:

- Direct memory: The HTTP client now consumes some direct memory. Operators running close to their `-XX:MaxDirectMemorySize` budget may need to increase it.
- Pooled buffers: Buffers are now pooled, so resident memory may appear higher than under Netty 3, even when idle. This is normal for a pooled allocator.

There are new configs that control the behavior of the HTTP client: `druid.global.http.connectTimeout`, `druid.global.http.allocator`, `druid.broker.http.connectTimeout`, and `druid.broker.http.allocator`. You can also set some Netty configs directly.

[#19567](https://github.com/apache/druid/pull/19567)

### Quality of service filtering for Coordinator

* Avoid creating a redundant Windows Job Object when SnapRAID is
   already running inside an existing job (such as under SnapRAID
   Daemon). This prevents potential execution failures of child
   processes (such as smartctl) on systems where nested job objects are
   not supported.
 * Skip disks on network or virtual filesystems (such as NFS, CIFS,
   FUSE, or tmpfs) in device operations like 'up', 'down', 'smart',
   and 'probe' on Linux, instead of failing with an error. If no
   physical device remains, the operation completes successfully with
   an informational message.

 * Enh [#21883](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21883): Handle corrupted pack files in `find --pack`
 * Enh [#21892](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21892): Make `repair snapshots --forget` remove broken snapshots
 * Enh [#21937](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21937): Reduce memory usage of the in-memory index

Details
-------

 * Security #22178: Fix ownership when `restore --ownership-by-name` cannot resolve names

   When restoring with `--ownership-by-name`, user or group names that could not be resolved on the restore host (or were not recorded in the snapshot) caused restic to change the owner of the restored file to UID/GID 0. Combined with restored setuid/setgid bits this could produce unintentional setuid-root files.

   Restic now instead falls back to the numeric UID/GID stored in the snapshot and prints a warning when a name cannot be resolved.

    [#22178](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22178) [#22185](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22185) 

 * Security #22180: Reject duplicate or out-of-order node names during `restore`

   A tree containing a symlink and a directory with the same name could let `restore` write through the symlink to files outside the restore target.

   Restic now rejects trees whose node names are not strictly increasing during restore and reports an error instead of restoring such a snapshot.

   Thanks to Mario Ramos (@marrionesa), calif.io, Zachariah Mithani (AploSec) and Manuel Riel (@m3nu) for reporting this.

    [#22180](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22180) [#22190](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22190) 

 * Bugfix #21977: Don't crash on truncated key or config file

   Restic previously crashed with a slice bounds panic when the repository contained a key or config file that was shorter than the encryption overhead, for example after an upload was interrupted. Since every command has to read a key file, the whole repository became unusable until the file was removed.

   This has now been fixed, and restic instead reports that the file is too short.

    [#21977](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21977) 

 * Bugfix #22007: Redact `swift` backend password in debug log output

   Restic could previously write the OpenStack Swift backend password in clear text to the debug log when debug logging was enabled. The password came from the environment variables `OS_PASSWORD` and `ST_KEY`. It is now redacted.

    [#22007](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22007) 

 * Bugfix #22051: Reject empty repository location files

   Previously, if the `--repository-file` option or `RESTIC_REPOSITORY_FILE` environment variable referred to a file that was either empty or contained only whitespace, restic used the current directory for the repository.

   This has now been fixed, and restic instead reports an error in this case.

    [#22051](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22051) [#22052](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22052) 

 * Bugfix #22085: Restore partially matching hard-linked files correctly

   When restoring over an existing file which had hard links and was partially different from the file in the snapshot, restic used to replace the file with an empty one but only restored the changed parts. Notable changes
---------------

- [PR #19862][kubevirt-bot] Bump libvirtxml to v1.12007.0 and fix the smmuv3 IOMMU ssidsize attribute, so Grace IOVirtualization VMIs get their SSID size and keep their IOMMU driver attributes when guest definition plugin hooks run.
- [PR #19771][kubevirt-bot] Fix VMIs with SR-IOV, GPU or PCI host devices failing to start when the Plugins feature gate is enabled and any Plugin exists in the cluster.
- [PR #19863][kubevirt-bot] Node hooks now fall back to the Plugin-level failureStrategy when they do not set their own, like launcher hooks. Plugins with spec.failureStrategy: Ignore no longer block VM start, stop or migration when one of their node hooks without its own failureStrategy fails.
- [PR #19743][kubevirt-bot] Fixed a virt-handler panic when a device plugin is restarted, which on nodes with host devices happened on every kubelet restart.
- [PR #19732][stu-gott] Live migrations are no longer scheduled from a node running an updated virt-handler onto a node that has not yet been updated, preventing migrations from getting stuck during a rolling upgrade.
- [PR #19690][kubevirt-bot] Beta: IncrementalBackup, and introduce backup.kubevirt.io/v1beta1
- [PR #19688][kubevirt-bot] CBT overlays are now keyed by volume and PVC name. Pointing a volume at a different PVC triggers a Full backup instead of an incorrect incremental.
- [PR #19294][alromeros] Offline incremental backup
- [PR #19492][caxu-rh] Fixed a bug that caused a gRPC connection to leak when virt-handler client initialization fails
- [PR #19574][noamasu] Guest writes are recovered when a VM starts after a virt-launcher crash during an External mode snapshot.
- [PR #19360][noamasu] VEP 321: add External mode VirtualMachineSnapshot
- [PR #19485][0xFelix] Exported OCI archives now contain the Image Index as a blob referenced from index.json with ref.name "latest", so pushing them creates an Image Index in the registry
- [PR #19550][Acedus] Memory dumps are attached as utility volumes and require the UtilityVolumes feature gate, which is promoted to Beta and enabled by default. VM snapshots and exports no longer include the memory dump PVC.
- [PR #19056][Acedus] VirtualMachineBackup no longer fails when a disk has lost the base checkpoint's bitmap; that disk is backed up in full and type is now reported per volume in `status.includedVolumes[].type`, replacing the removed `status.type`.
- [PR #19511][nirdothan] NetworkDevicesWithDRA Feature Gate is now in Beta stage
- [PR #17135][lyarwood] Add Alpha UEFI Secure Boot support for ARM64 guests through the ARM64SecureBoot and FirmwareAutoSelection feature gates. Requires CentOS Stream 10 virt-launcher images with suitable QEMU, libvirt, and edk2 firmware. Supports persistent EFI state through existing backend storage.
- [PR #19590][lyarwood] Build KubeVirt with go 1.26.10
- [PR #19066][0xFelix] The io.kubevirt.disk.name annotation of exported OCI artifacts now carries the volume name from the VM instead of the PersistentVolumeClaim name
- [PR #19228][Sreeja1725] Alpha: Add CPUsWithDRA to provision dedicated VMI CPUs via a DRA CPU driver instead of kubelet's CPU manager.
- [PR #19572][orelmisan] The pod-status VMI network interface info source is now reported for interfaces whose device is ready in the pod (DRA-backed, and Multus-backed secondary interfaces), when the NetworkDevicesWithDRA feature gate is enabled.
- [PR #19173][alromeros] Declarative VirtualMachineState
- [PR #19410][Acedus] HostDisk volumes are no longer eligible for changed block tracking.
- [PR #19520][noamasu] Use a memory-backed emptyDir for the hotplug mount root to support mount propagation.
- [PR #19435][awels] Cleanup CBT overlays when disabling CBT
- [PR #19382][mhenriks] ContainerPath volumes graduate to beta
- [PR #19240][vladikr] virt-launcher-monitor is rewritten in C to reduce memory footprint to about 2Mi
- [PR #19064][0xFelix] Fixed a bug where a VirtualMachineExport of a VM with two claims whose names differ only in dots would never complete
- [PR #18249][dsanatar] IOThread Virtqueue Mapping for virtio-scsi
- [PR #19546][dasionov] Renamed the alpha feature gate for mdev-based vGPU live migration from VGPULiveMigration to MDevVGPULiveMigration.
- [PR #19534][caxu-rh] Fixed a bug where a Unix socket listener may be left open if an error occurs while setting file ownership on the socket
- [PR #19490][awels] Only add virt-handler migration identity to synchronization controller if proxy is enabled.
- [PR #19470][avlitman] Added a has_panic_device label (true/false) to the kubevirt_vmi_info metric
- [PR #19409][Acedus] Live migration of CBT-enabled VMs creates the target's CBT overlays from the source's domain, and unplugging a volume removes its CBT overlay regardless of the VMI's CBT state.
- [PR #19403][iholder101] Add PreBoot and PreMigrationSource sidecar launcher hook points for plugins.

## Highlights

Flux v2.10.1 is a patch release that fixes credential caching across the controllers, so changes to the `credential.auth.fluxcd.io/username` and `gcp.auth.fluxcd.io/workload-identity-provider` ServiceAccount annotations take effect on the next reconcile instead of continuing to use the previously cached authenticator until it expires or the controller restarts. It also resolves the default decryption ServiceAccount lazily for Kustomizations that only use Age or PGP keys, restores authentication to registries whose token service runs on a private address and after same-host HTTP to HTTPS redirects by updating ORAS to v2.7.0, and fixes Git checkouts that deleted the target of a relative symlink or got permanently stuck when the push branch removed a file that relative symlinks point to. Users are encouraged to upgrade for the best experience.

ℹ️ Please follow the [Upgrade Procedure for Flux v2.7+](https://github.com/fluxcd/flux2/discussions/5572) for a smooth upgrade from Flux v2.6 to the latest version.

Fixes:
- Fix the credentials cache key so changes to the credential username or the GCP workload identity provider take effect on the next reconcile (helm-controller, kustomize-controller, source-controller, notification-controller, image-reflector-controller, image-automation-controller)
- Fix resolving the default ServiceAccount for providers that don't use one (source-controller, image-reflector-controller, image-automation-controller)
- Resolve the default decryption ServiceAccount lazily, only when a cloud KMS or Vault backend is used (kustomize-controller)
- Restore authentication to registries whose token service runs on a private address and after same-host HTTP to HTTPS redirects by updating ORAS to v2.7.0 (source-controller)
- Fix Git checkouts deleting the target of a relative symlink when the checked-out revision removes the symlink (source-controller)
- Fix Git checkouts getting stuck when the push branch removes a file that relative symlinks point to (image-automation-controller)
- Delete the reconcile duration metric series for objects that no longer exist (kustomize-controller)

Improvements:
- Remove leftover object-level workload identity log message (helm-controller, kustomize-controller, source-controller, notification-controller, image-reflector-controller, image-automation-controller)

## Changes

### Breaking changes

- **`curl` removed from the kubectl shell image.** `curl` and its libraries were removed from the kubectl shell image to cut the OS-package vulnerabilities they brought in. Upgraded installs keep their existing kubectl shell image until it is updated with `--kubectl-shell-image` (or `KUBECTL_SHELL_IMAGE`) or through `PUT /api/settings`; new installs get the new image. Anyone who runs commands or scripts in the kubectl shell that call `curl` now gets `curl: not found`. Use `wget` instead, which is still included through busybox, or point `--kubectl-shell-image` at your own image if you need `curl`
- **Stacks can only use networks the user has access to.** Non-administrators could previously attach containers and stacks to Docker networks they had no access to, which bypassed network access control. Now, a non-administrator's Compose or Swarm stack that uses such a network (as `external`, through `network_mode`, or as a build `network`) fails on start, update, Git redeploy and auto-update. A container create that names the network fails with "forbidden to join this network". This mostly affects stacks that use a shared network created by an administrator or outside Portainer. Grant the users or teams access to the network through its access control, or have an administrator deploy the stack
- **In-app updates pull a specific version.** In-app updates on Docker standalone and Swarm used to pull the `latest` tag, which on Kubernetes could report success without changing anything. They now pull the exact Portainer version tag, for example `portainer/portainer-ee:2.45.4`. Installs that pull images through a private registry mirror or proxy need that version tag mirrored, or the update fails. `POST /api/system/update` now returns 500 when no newer version is available or the release feed can't be reached
- **GitOps source connection tests need write access.** A user with only read access to a GitOps source could run its connection test against a different repository URL, which sent the source's stored credentials there. In CE and BE, `POST /gitops/sources/{id}/test` now requires write access to the source to change any field other than name or interval, and read-only users get a 403 if they try. Give users who need to test with different settings write access to the source
- **Kubernetes permissions follow each user's role (since 2.45.0).** Portainer used to carry out some Kubernetes actions with the agent's cluster-wide permissions, so a user's role wasn't always enforced. It now uses each user's own ServiceAccount, limited to the namespaces their role covers.
    - **Who is affected:** users other than administrators and environment administrators.
    - **What fails:** these actions now fail with a Kubernetes "forbidden" error if they include cluster-scoped resources, custom resources that Portainer's roles don't grant (for example a cert-manager `Certificate`), or resources in namespaces the user can't access:
        - manifest stack deploys, updates and removals;
        - Git and webhook redeploys;
        - application rolling restarts;
        - Helm charts deployed from Git.
    - **Stacks created before the upgrade** are affected when they're updated or redeployed.
    - **Access outside their namespaces:** Operators, Helpdesk, Read-only and Standard users also lose access they previously had outside their namespaces, including to system namespaces.
    - **Read-only and Helpdesk users can no longer view secret values** in the UI or the API, or read secrets with kubectl or a kubeconfig. Helm release values, manifests and notes are hidden from them, and the helm CLI no longer works to list releases.
    - **What to do:** for deployments that fail with “forbidden”, have an administrator deploy those resources, or grant the extra permissions in the cluster. For Read-only and Helpdesk users who need to read secrets, give them a role that allows it in that namespace, such as Standard user or Operator. See [Kubernetes roles and bindings](https://docs.portainer.io/advanced/kubernetes-roles-and-bindings) for the current roles and how to extend them.
   
### Improved features

#### Security

- Fixed `GET /stacks` returning stacks from environments the user cannot access. Non-admin users could list Public stacks, including their stored environment variables and Git configuration, on any environment; the list is now filtered by environment access as well as stack access control
- Fixed non-administrators being able to mount the Docker socket through the Compose `use_api_socket` option. The stack validator now rejects it when bind mounts are disabled for regular users
- Fixed the Compose stack validator skipping services that use `profiles:` and not checking `include:`. Non-administrator stack restrictions now apply to every service whatever its profile and `include` is rejected when bind mounts are disabled for regular users; in BE, the SSRF policy checks on build-context and image-registry URLs, including for Edge stacks, also cover profiled services

## Actor and workflow calls kept failing after a pod IP was reused by a different app

### Problem

The sidecar keeps one gRPC connection per remote address for calls to other sidecars, such as actor invocation and workflow calls between apps.
The mTLS credentials of a connection pin the namespace and app ID of the peer it was created for, and gRPC reuses them every time the connection reconnects.
The connection pool was keyed by address only.
When Kubernetes gave the IP of a stopped pod to a pod of a different app, the sidecar kept using the connection created for the previous app.
Every handshake failed with `unexpected SPIFFE ID`, and every actor or workflow call to the new app on that address failed with `Unavailable`.

### Impact

You were affected if mTLS is enabled, your apps call actors or workflows on a remote app, and the IP of a pod was reused by a pod of a different app.
Calls from a sidecar to that address kept failing until the sidecar stopped calling it for 3 minutes (`DAPR_GRPC_MAX_CONN_IDLE`) or the target pod got a new IP.
With steady traffic, that did not happen. Calls to other pods of the same app were not affected.
Deleting the pod that received the reused IP recovered it.

### Root Cause

The pool looked up an existing connection by address, and the identity the connection expects was not part of the lookup.
Before Dapr 1.15 the actor call path closed the connection when a call failed with `Unavailable`, which hid the problem.
Since 1.15 it does not, and nothing else closes a connection that is in use.
Service invocation and the gRPC proxy still close the connection on `Unavailable`, so they recovered.

### Solution

The connection pool is now keyed by address, namespace and app ID.
A sidecar that finds a different app at an address it has used before dials a new connection with the credentials for that app.
Connections to the same address, namespace and app ID are still shared.
When a sidecar dials a new connection to an address, it also closes the idle connections it holds there for other apps, which can no longer succeed. Connections that are in use are left to finish.

## Actor sidecars stopped becoming ready after a sidecar without an actor state store joined

### Problem

The Placement service could stop sending placement tables in a namespace.
After that, every new sidecar in the namespace waited for its table and never became ready, and actor placement in the namespace stopped changing.
The Placement service did not recover on its own.

### Impact

You were affected if an app declares actor types but has no actor state store, and its sidecar connects to Placement when only one other sidecar with actors is connected in the namespace.
New sidecars in that namespace did not become ready until the Placement leader restarted.

### Root Cause

A sidecar that declares actor types but has no actor state store reports its host to Placement twice when it connects.
Placement answers each report with a copy of the placement table sent to that sidecar only, and ignores the sidecar's acknowledgements of that copy.
After the second copy, Placement counted the sidecar's acknowledgements as part of a namespace-wide update that was not running.
With two sidecars in the namespace, that was enough to finish the phantom update, and Placement asked the other sidecar to unlock with no timeout set.
The other sidecar ignored that request because it was out of sequence, and Placement waited for its answer indefinitely.

### Solution

Placement now counts an acknowledgement only when it is for the current step of the update.

## Workflows and activities with per-name concurrency limits stalled in the Scheduler

### Problem

When a workflow or activity name had a per-name concurrency limit and the matching global limit was also set, work waiting for a free slot was not started when a running instance completed.
It stayed queued until some unrelated workflow or activity of the same type completed.

### Impact

You were affected on Dapr 1.19.0 and 1.19.1 if, in the `workflow` section of the Dapr Configuration, you set a per-name limit together

## What's Changed

> ℹ️ **Scheduled jobs are now supported.** A job is a one-shot unit of work declared in the top-level `jobs:` element of your Compose file, run on demand or on a schedule. 
Scheduling needs **Docker Engine 29.10 or later with the jobs extension enabled** (it is off by default: `dockerd --extension-enable org.mobyproject.jobs.v0`). Manual jobs keep working on any engine, and projects that declare no jobs are unaffected.

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres
jobs:
  backup:
    image: backup-tool
    depends_on: [db]
    triggers:
      schedule:
        - cron: "0 3 * * *"
```

> * `docker compose up` (or `create`) registers the scheduled jobs with the engine, which fires them on its own clock; `docker compose down` removes them. On an engine without jobs support, `up` refuses a project with scheduled jobs before creating anything.
> * `docker compose run backup` triggers a job right away: its dependencies start first, its logs are streamed and its exit code is returned. On an engine without jobs support, it runs as a one-off service with a warning, as before.

## Bumping ClickHouse to 26.8 requires AVX2

> [!WARNING]
> If you're running on CPUs released before 2013, this release may be a blocker for you. Please read the ClickHouse upgrade notes below carefully before you upgrade.

ClickHouse is one of the components affected by [CVE-2026-116366](https://www.cve.org/cverecord?id=CVE-2026-116366), a vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user with network access to execute arbitrary code on the ClickHouse Server. ClickHouse has fixed it in v26.10.3.7, but the upstream project has not backported the fix to the 25.x line. That's an upstream decision, not one we made. Because of that, we're moving to the newer [26.8 release](https://github.com/getsentry/self-hosted/pull/4614) instead.

This newer release requires the host CPU to support the AVX1 and AVX2 instruction sets on x86 platforms. ClickHouse's upstream reasoning is that these instructions give the compiler's auto-vectorizer more room to optimize beyond SSE. You can read more in the [ClickHouse issue](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/40459).

To check, run this on a Linux or other POSIX host:

```bash
grep 'avx2' /proc/cpuinfo
```

If the output is non-empty, you're good to go. If it's empty, you'll need to upgrade your machine before you can run this release. If you're on a non-Linux host or inside some virtualized environments, `/proc/cpuinfo` may not be available or reliable, so check your platform's documentation for an equivalent.

Backing up your ClickHouse data before a major version bump is a good idea. It isn't strictly required, but it's cheap insurance.

## Interesting things to try

If you're looking to experiment on your self-hosted Sentry instance, these flags are for the brave wanderers.

- **Low priority queries:** `organizations:low-priority-queries` shows a toggle that runs queries against a smaller "explore" dataset. Results come back faster, but they won't be 100% accurate.
- **Browser reports ingestion:** `organizations:browser-report-ingestion` is an experimental flag that enables ingestion of [[Network Error Logging (NEL)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Network_Error_Logging) browser reports into Sentry. See the [Relay PR](https://github.com/getsentry/relay/pull/6592) for more context.

MISP 2.5.52 Released – Major security release

MISP 2.5.52 is a **major security release**. It contains more than fifty security fixes and a
long list of hardening changes, covering access control across the API and the UI,
synchronisation and feeds, protected event signing, authentication, exports, and a number of
cross-site scripting issues in the user interface. **We strongly recommend that all users
upgrade as soon as possible.**

Please read the [upgrade notes](#before-you-upgrade) below before upgrading: MISP's Python
dependencies now need **Python 3.11 or newer**, and a few security fixes change behaviour that
some setups rely on.

## Thank you

This release would not have been possible without the people who took the time to look closely
at MISP and report what they found. Our warmest thanks go to:

*   **ENISA**, for their in-depth security review of MISP, which accounts for the bulk of the

*   **Jeroen Pinoy**, for their reports.
*   **Francois-Xavier Stellamans** from the NATO Cyber Security Centre (with OpenAI Daybreak
    support, using GPT5.6-Cyber), for their reports.

Responsible disclosure like theirs makes MISP safer for the whole community.

## Before you upgrade

*   **Python 3.11 or newer is required** for MISP's Python environment. MISP now pins
    PyMISP 3.0.0, which, together with the matching misp-stix release, no longer installs on
    Python 3.10. Ubuntu 22.04 ships Python 3.10 by default: install a newer Python, rebuild
    MISP's virtual environment with it, and point `MISP.python_bin` at the new interpreter.
*   **Apply the database updates** (log in as an admin, or run
    `sudo -u www-data app/Console/cake Admin runUpdates`) and restart PHP-FPM and the background
    workers when asked. This release brings three migrations: a repair of Redis
    values stored PHP-serialised, the removal of auth keys and settings left behind by deleted
    users, and the clean-up of stale sharing group references on collections.
*   **Reverse proxies:** when `MISP.log_client_ip_header` is set, MISP now takes the client
    address from the trusted (right-most) end of the header. If your instance sits behind more
    than one proxy, list them in the new **`MISP.trusted_proxies`** setting. The resolved address
    is the one used for auth key IP restrictions, brute-force protection and the logs.
*   **Password reset e-mails** are only sent when `MISP.baseurl` or `MISP.external_baseurl` is
    configured; MISP no longer builds the link from the request's `Host` header.
*   **CertAuth** only accepts client certificates that the web server has verified
    (`SSL_CLIENT_VERIFY=SUCCESS`).
*   **Compressed request bodies** are only decoded for authenticated users, gzip only (brotli
    and zstd are no longer accepted), up to the new **`Security.max_decompressed_size`**
    setting. The same limit applies to feed and sync responses once decompressed; it defaults to
    the PHP memory limit, and it needs to be at least as large as the JSON of your largest
    events.
*   **External authentication** (LDAP, Shibboleth and the other backends): while it is
    configured, only site admins can change a user's login e-mail.

## Removed

*   The recovery of deleted events from the logs (`events/restoreDeletedEvents`,
    `events/recoverEvent` and its CLI command).
*   The STIX sightings upload (`POST /sightings/add/stix`), which relied on a Python 2 script
    and could not work on any supported install.
*   The legacy STIX 1 importer: STIX 1 imports now go through misp-stix.
*   The unused `GnuPG.restrict_server_signing_to_host_org` setting.

## New

*   **2.5 <-> 3.x synchronisation:** MISP 2.5 instances can now sync with MISP 3.x instances,
    and the version-dependent sync features (proposals, organisation rules, protected events,
    sighting searches) stay available against a 3.x remote.
*   **Gathering feeds:** misp-modules gathering modules can be used as a feed source. The module
    produces a standard MISP feed, which MISP streams through its existing feed importer. See
    `design-doc/misp-modules/gathering-feeds.md` for the setup.
*   **Per-module execution timeouts** for misp-modules.
*   **OIDC refresh tokens** are stored encrypted when `Security.encryption_key` is set; existing
    plaintext tokens keep working.
*   **Overmind interface:** a Timeline tab and a galaxy matrix card in the event view, an
    Ownership & Distribution card, IDs and UUIDs in the page header, an icon on geolocation
    objects, a zoom and filter mode for the correlation graph, a reworked REST client,
    entity extraction when editing a report, bulk hard and soft deletes on the attribute,
    object and galaxy cluster indexes, an improved onboarding tutorial, and refreshed views
    throughout.

## Changes

*   PyMISP 3.0.0 and the latest misp-stix; CakePHP, galaxies, objects, taxonomies and
    warninglists updated to their latest versions.
*   CIDR correlation is skipped for very broad prefixes (IPv4 shorter than /8, IPv6 shorter than
    /16).
*   Deleting a user now also deletes their auth keys and user settings.
*   The attribute form recommends object templates instead of composite hash types.
*   Event report previews load only the elements they cite.

## Fixes

*   **Workflows:** "IF :: Distribution" evaluates every attribute, object attributes included;
    the "IF :: Tag" all-of conditions no longer depend on tag order or on a tag repeated across
    attributes; built-in modules take precedence over a misp-module using the same id.
*   **Synchronisation:** pulls no longer stop early on index pages shortened by hidden protected
    events, and empty index pages are no longer cached (#11154); protected events can be
