## Fleet 4.95.0 (Nov 16, 2026)

### Changes that may require action

- Removed fleetd's built-in Nudge integration. Fleet no longer sends Nudge settings to fleetd for hosts on macOS 13 and older, which are no longer supported. Hosts on macOS 14 and later continue to get OS update enforcement via DDM. To keep using Nudge, deploy it with the Nudge Fleet-maintained app. Learn how in the [Nudge guide](https://fleetdm.com/guides/enforce-os-updates-on-macos-with-nudge).
- Changed `fleetctl gitops` and the batch APIs to reject configuration profiles, scripts, reports, and labels whose names differ only by letter case, accents, or trailing spaces. Previously these were accepted and only one of them was saved. Rename the duplicates before upgrading.
- Changed `fleetctl gitops` on Fleet Free to return an error for custom EST and Smallstep certificate authorities, which require Fleet Premium. Previously they were ignored. Remove them from your YAML before upgrading.
- Changed Windows BitLocker key escrow to require `server.private_key`. Deployments that turned on Windows disk encryption without one should set it when upgrading.
- Changed the Technician role to only run saved scripts. Running ad hoc scripts (`script_contents`) through the API and `fleetctl run-script` now fails for Technicians.

### IT Admins

- Added Okta conditional access for Windows hosts (Fleet Premium): a new `$FLEET_VAR_CONDITIONAL_ACCESS_SCEP_URL` variable for Windows SCEP profiles, a `GET /api/v1/fleet/conditional_access/idp/windows/profiles` endpoint, and a new Okta conditional access page in Settings that shows the macOS and Windows profiles.
- Added `PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/fleet/hosts/:id/google_device_id` endpoints (Fleet Premium) to bind an iOS, iPadOS, or Android host to its device ID in Google and to remove that binding, for Google conditional access. Once set, a host's Google device ID can only be removed with `DELETE`, and each ID can only be bound to one host.
- Added a built-in MCP server to Fleet Premium at `/api/v1/fleet/mcp`, on by default and turned off with `server_settings.mcp_disabled`. AI tools connect with an API-only user's token and only get the tools that user's API endpoints allow.
- Added a "Deadline" option for macOS Fleet-maintained app patch policies. When the app is open, Fleet Desktop tells the end user 1 hour before the deadline and again 5 minutes before, then closes and updates the app. Requires Fleet Desktop 1.5.0.
- Added patch deadline settings (days and time) per fleet and for "Unassigned" in Software > Library > Settings, the API, and GitOps. Deadlines use each host's local time. The default is Tuesday at 17:00.
- Added support for assigning multiple VPP tokens to a fleet. A VPP token on "All fleets" is now available alongside fleet-specific tokens. When adding an App Store app, you choose the VPP token, and each app installs with the token it was added from.
- Added EJBCA as a certificate authority type (Fleet Premium). Add it in **Settings > Integrations > Certificate authorities**, with the API, or with GitOps (`org_settings.certificate_authorities.ejbca`), and use the `$FLEET_VAR_EJBCA_DATA_<name>` and `$FLEET_VAR_EJBCA_PASSWORD_<name>` variables in the PKCS#12 payload of a macOS, iOS, or iPadOS configuration profile to deliver a certificate to each host.
- Added Google Cloud Certificate Authority Service (CAS) as a certificate authority type, so Linux hosts can get certificates from it through the request certificate API.
- Added support for `$FLEET_VAR_HOST_UUID` and the `$FLEET_VAR_HOST_END_USER_IDP_*` variables in a DigiCert certificate authority's common name, seat ID, and UPN. Certificates that use an IdP variable are reissued when the host's IdP values change.
- Added the `$FLEET_VAR_HOST_END_USER_IDP_EXTERNAL_ID` variable, which resolves to the host end user's SCIM `externalId`, for configuration profiles, declarations, scripts, managed app configurations, certificate templates, and host name templates.
- Added API endpoints that use AI to generate a configuration profile, or its name and description, from plain-language instructions, checking the profile the way Fleet does when it is added.
- Combined assets into the configuration profiles list in Controls > OS settings. Assets are now added from the "Advanced" button next to "Add profile".
- Added `macos_enable_bootstrap_package_during_manual_enrollment` and `macos_enable_bootstrap_package_during_migration` setup experience settings to install a configured bootstrap package on a manual enrollment and MDM migration respectively.
- Changed Windows Autopilot devices with a placeholder hardware serial (for example "Default string") to appear in Fleet as pending hosts. Every Autopilot device is matched to its pending host by its Autopilot device ID when fleetd enrolls, so devices that share a serial each stay a single host. Requires fleetd v1.64.0.

- Added Parrot OS as a recognized Linux platform. 1. Security: values sent by the CA can no longer run shell commands. A single
quote in a URL from the CA (finalize, order, cert or account URL) broke out of
the quoting in the saved conf file, and a challenge token or URL holding `#`
could make acme.sh source a local file as a DNS hook. Challenge tokens and
URLs from the CA are now validated. Exploiting either needs a malicious CA or
a broken TLS connection to the CA. Reported by Martin Arlitt and Srini
Seethapathy (Corelight).
2. `--insecure` now applies to the current run only and is no longer saved to
account.conf. A value saved by an older version is ignored and removed; see the
wiki [Note on --insecure](https://github.com/acmesh-official/acme.sh/wiki/Options-and-Params).
3. Signed requests are retried on transport errors, and wget2 is supported.
4. `--install-cert` can now update the pre/post/renew hooks
([#7346](https://github.com/acmesh-official/acme.sh/pull/7346)).
5. Conf files: a write that changes nothing is skipped, and the file is kept
intact when a write fails
([#7278](https://github.com/acmesh-official/acme.sh/pull/7278)). The email
given on the command line no longer overwrites the one in account.conf.
6. New DNS providers: bergdns.at, MVMNET, Public Internet (dns_pblin), Abion,
PrimeDNS, ConnByte, hosttech, Domain Chief, NameOcean, MizbanCloud, Timeweb
(dns_timeweb_host). Cloudflare supports IDN domains, and Simply.com uses
Bearer auth.
7. New deploy hooks: Nginx Proxy Manager / NPMplus, Redfish BMCs, HP printers
(hp_ews), pfSense (pfREST), Proxmox Mail Gateway. deploy/ssh supports pfx and
stops at the first failed step; synology_dsm can generate 2FA codes from
SYNO_TOTP_SECRET.
8. New notify hook: Healthchecks.io.
9. Docker: set-default, update-account-key, list-profiles and
make-dns-persist-value are exposed as commands.
10. A lot of bug fixes.

ClamAV 1.5.5 is a patch release with the following fixes:

- [CVE-2026-76422](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76422):
  Fixed Rust-to-C logging so rendered messages are passed as data rather than
  as C format strings. Crafted input could otherwise cause a crash, disclose
  process memory, or corrupt memory when attacker-controlled text was logged.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.105.0 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to Feng Xue for identifying this issue.

- [CVE-2026-76411](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76411):
  Fixed URL canonicalization length accounting that could write beyond a
  stack buffer while scanning crafted email with full-hash phishing database
  entries loaded.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.94 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to Feng Xue for identifying this issue.

- [CVE-2026-76415](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76415):
  Fixed yC executable unpacker offset validation that could underflow and read
  beyond a heap buffer while scanning a malformed file.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.96 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to Nebula Security for identifying this issue.

- [CVE-2026-76414](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76414):
  Bounded CHM directory traversal to prevent cyclic directory data from
  causing an infinite scan loop and denial of service.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.100.0 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to Nebula Security for identifying this issue.

- [CVE-2026-76416](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76416):
  Validated InstallShield file table counts and offsets, and applied scan time
  limits, to prevent malformed archives from pinning a scan worker.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.96 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to Nebula Security for identifying this issue.

- [CVE-2026-76417](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76417):
  Fixed OLE2 property traversal recursion accounting to prevent a deeply
  nested crafted document from exhausting the process stack.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.71 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to Nebula Security for identifying this issue.

- [CVE-2026-76421](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76421):
  Validated LZX match offsets before narrowing them to prevent a malformed CHM
  archive from causing an out-of-bounds heap write.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.80 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to Feng Xue and XGPT of ThreatBook for identifying this issue.

- [CVE-2026-76430](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76430):
  Bounded UPX decompression and PE rebuilding output to prevent malformed
  packed executables from causing out-of-bounds heap writes.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.94.1 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to Feng Xue and, independently, Nicola Ruaro for identifying this
  issue.

- [CVE-2026-76516](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76516):
  Enforced file-count and scan-size limits before XAR extraction writes to
  prevent crafted archives from exhausting temporary storage.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.98 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to DieHardMan 300 for identifying this issue.

- [CVE-2026-76515](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-76515):
  Bounded OLE2 directory-chain traversal and applied scan time limits to
  prevent crafted documents from causing excessive CPU use.

  This issue affects ClamAV 0.98.1 through 1.5.4.
  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

  Thank you to Ziyue Wang, Liyi Zhou, Strick, Maurice, and Chenchen Yu of
  Disproof AI Lab, University of Sydney, for identifying this issue.

- Tightened the built-in HTML file type signatures so XML and custom elements
  whose names merely start with an HTML tag name are not classified as HTML.

- Sigtool now retries after a delay when building a database archive whose MD5
  hash begins with `00`, preserving compatibility with ClamAV 1.1 through 1.4.

- Restored `clamsubmit` sample submissions after the service changed its
  presigned-upload endpoint from GET to POST. The client now preserves the
  session, CSRF token, and referer, handles optional S3 ACL fields, and reports
  HTTP or malformed-response errors instead of crashing.

  The fix is included in 1.4.7 and 1.5.5.

- Improved compatibility with OpenSSL 4 and reduced hashing overhead by reusing
  digest implementations fetched from a long-lived private library context.
  Also read opaque `ASN1_TIME` values through supported accessors instead of
  accessing OpenSSL internals directly.

  Thank you to Seweryn Chlewicki and Sebastian Andrzej Siewior for these
  improvements.

- Upgraded the Rust `anyhow` and `rand` dependencies to resolve the
  RUSTSEC-2026-0190 and RUSTSEC-2026-0097 advisories.

This release fixes a large set of access control issues across the app, the external REST API (`/api/v1/`) and published boards, and hardens sign-in, sessions and deployments. Self-hosted instances should upgrade.

**Access control and tenant isolation**

- Scoped published board detail routes to the workspace and project in the URL. Previously any signed-in user could read, change or delete another workspace's published boards.
- Blocked workspace admins from moving a member into another workspace, as an admin, by sending a `workspace` field when updating the member. Member updates now accept only the role.
- Limited listing, viewing and deleting project invitations to project admins.
- Scoped work item comment and relation creation to the project in the URL. Previously a member of one project could comment on or relate a work item in another project or workspace, and the response returned that work item's details.
- Bound work item, module and cycle IDs in the URL to the URL's project when creating related objects.
- Required an active Admin or Member role in a draft's project to create, update or convert workspace drafts, and checked the draft's cycle, modules, state, labels, assignees, parent and estimate against that project.
- Checked page access on every live collaboration connection. Previously only the first connection to load a page was checked, so any signed-in user could join an open page by its ID. Guests now join read-only, and title changes are saved with the editing user's own credentials.
- Limited project entity search to active members of the project. Previously any workspace member could list another project's members.
- Required project leads and default assignees to be active workspace members, in the app and the external API.
- Bound project cover uploads to a project in the URL's workspace that the caller administers.

- Required project membership on every workspace-level asset route, including upload, download and duplication, and stopped the external ID lookup from returning asset IDs from other projects.

### Security fixes

* Strengthen SSRF protection for webhooks and web link previews:
  * Connect to the IP address that passed validation, so a DNS change between the check and the request (DNS rebinding) can no longer reach a private network.
  * Block more non-public address ranges, such as carrier-grade NAT, benchmarking, and documentation networks.
  * The `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` and `EXTERNAL_LINK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` options still turn off these checks.
* Reject empty LDAP passwords. Active Directory accepts them as unauthenticated binds, which allowed LDAP users without two-factor authentication to be logged in through the API without a password.
* Apply brute-force protection to two-factor authentication codes:
  * Invalid codes count toward account lockout.
  * The failed login counter is reset only after a valid code is entered.
* Invalidate the login CAPTCHA after each attempt so it cannot be reused.
* Enforce comment visibility in notifications and feeds:
  * Users are notified only about comments their role allows them to see.
  * Project notification channels and activity feeds receive only comments visible to standard users.
* Prevent disclosure of data from other projects:
  * Board tooltips and the "close all tasks" dialog now check that the column and swimlane belong to the project.
  * Public task views no longer show links to tasks in other projects.
  * Mention suggestions no longer list members of projects the user cannot access.
* Validate task references and permissions:
  * Check that the column, swimlane, and category belong to the task's project when tasks are created, edited, moved, imported, made recurring, or bulk changed.
  * Allow only users who can be assigned in the project to be set as task assignee, including in CSV imports.
  * Require permission to create tasks in the destination column when copying or moving a task to another project, and list only the destinations that pass.
* Restrict iCal feeds:
  * Remove assignee and creator email addresses.
  * Exclude tasks from projects the user was removed from, and from inactive projects.

### Improvements

* Add an optional iCal feed that also lists open tasks without dates as to-dos (`VTODO`):
  * Use the new "iCal feed with undated tasks" link on the project and user sharing pages, or add `todo=1` to an existing feed URL.

### Bug fixes

* Fix several iCal feed issues:
  * Write dates in UTC and make sure every event ends after it starts, as required by RFC 5545.
  * Detect all-day events using the timezone of the feed owner or the application, instead of the server.
  * Prevent tasks from appearing twice, and stop listing every open task without due date when the creation date is used as the start date.
  * Use globally unique event identifiers and the task modification date as `DTSTAMP`.
  * Fix the empty organizer email, the escaping of URLs, quotes, and parameters, and the missing final line break.
  * Use absolute task URLs, and make links in task descriptions of project feeds work for readers without an account.
* Fix "database is locked" errors with SQLite when several requests update the session at the same time.
* Fix a fatal error when the comment or email forms are opened in a new tab instead of the modal dialog.
* Keep the task time estimate when the "Add a subtask and activate the timer when moving a task to another column" action creates a subtask.
* Show time spent with two decimal places.
* Remove remaining PHP 8.5 deprecation warnings.

### Maintenance

* Pin tool versions and container images in the GitHub Actions workflows.

### Dependencies and build

* Replace third-party libraries with built-in implementations:
  * `eluceo/ical` for iCalendar feeds
  * `phpqrcode` for 2FA QR codes, which are now rendered as SVG
  * `gregwar/captcha` for the login CAPTCHA
  * `christian-riesen/otp` for TOTP codes

* Remove unused dependencies: `symfony/stopwatch`, `symfony/finder`, `doctrine/instantiator`, and the Symfony polyfills for ctype, mbstring, PHP 7.3, and PHP 8.0.

# 3.3.21

3.3.21 is a security hardening release. Pad socket.io connections now only use the visitor's cookies when they come from Etherpad's own pages. It also fixes pads embedded cross-site over plain http and an intermittent 404 on LibreOffice exports. Upgrading is recommended.

### Security

- **Collaboration — pad socket.io connections only use the visitor's cookies when they come from Etherpad's own pages (#8514).** A pad socket identifies the visitor from the cookies the browser sends with the handshake: the author token, an HTTP API group session and, with `requireAuthentication`, the login session. Browsers send those cookies with handshakes from any page on the same site, for example another subdomain of your domain. The pad page now fetches a short token from `GET /pad-socket-token` and sends it with the handshake, and same-origin connections are recognised from `Sec-Fetch-Site`. A pad socket opened by a page on another origin still connects, but its cookies are ignored, so it gets a fresh anonymous author with no group session and no login. Plugin hooks don't see those cookies or the login on such a socket either. Clients that send no `Origin` header, such as the `pad` CLI, bots and load tests, are not affected. Reported by @brx-zyy.

### Upgrade notes

- No configuration change is needed, including behind a reverse proxy that rewrites the `Host` header and for pads embedded in an iframe on another site: an embedded pad is an Etherpad page, so its socket comes from Etherpad's own origin. The check the pad page relies on does not depend on `Host`, `trustProxy` or `publicURL`.
- New setting `socketIo.crossOriginPadSockets` decides what happens to a pad socket opened by another origin: `"anonymous"` (default) ignores its cookies, `"reject"` refuses the connection and `"allow"` keeps the old behaviour. An unknown value logs an error and falls back to `"reject"`.
- New setting `socketIo.padAllowedOrigins` lists extra `scheme://host[:port]` origins whose pages may open pad sockets with the visitor's cookies. Origins in `socketIo.allowedOrigins` are trusted for pads too.
- If your integration sets the `sessionID` cookie itself, give it a `Path` that also covers `/pad-socket-token` (normally `Path=/`).

### Notable fixes

- **Embedding — a pad embedded cross-site over plain http loads again (#8515, #8513).** The browser rejects the prefs cookie in that case (`SameSite=None` needs `Secure`), and the pad then failed to finish loading. The pad now keeps its prefs in memory when the cookie can't be read or written. It loads with default prefs, and settings changed during the visit apply until reload.
- **Export — LibreOffice exports no longer intermittently fail with a 404 (#8517).** The converted file could be deleted while it was still being sent. The temp files are now removed only after the response has been sent, and also when sending fails.

### Other changes

- Dependency updates, including mssql 12.7.16, express-rate-limit 8.7.5, jose 6.2.18 and @tanstack/react-query 5.108.0.

## 5.63.0 (2026-11-18)

### ⚠️ Changes to be aware of

#### Some filters that used to return every entry now return 400

A plain object as an operator's operand on a scalar or JSON field, `id` or `documentId` (for example `filters[meta][$eq][a]=1`) used to drop the condition and return every entry. It now returns a 400 `ValidationError`. REST lists longer than the `strapi::query` middleware's `arrayLimit` (100 by default), such as `filters[id][$in]` with 101 ids, now also return this 400. To accept longer lists, replace `'strapi::query'` in `config/middlewares` with `{ name: 'strapi::query', config: { arrayLimit: 500 } }`.

([#28541](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28541)) · [docs](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/configurations/middlewares#query)

#### Long `$or` and `$and` lists now return 400

A REST `$or` or `$and` list longer than `arrayLimit` (100 by default), or one with an index of 100 or more such as `filters[$or][100]`, used to drop the condition and return every entry. It now returns a 400 `ValidationError`. Raise `arrayLimit` as above if you need longer lists. An object operand such as `filters[$or][title]=x` now returns 400 instead of a server error.

([#28563](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28563))

#### Empty `$in` and `$notIn` filters are now applied

A filter such as `{ id: { $in: [] } }` used to be stripped, so the query returned every entry. It now returns none, and `$notIn: []` returns every entry. If your code builds `$in` lists that can be empty, check the results it now gets.

([#27850](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/27850))

#### `$null` and `$notNull` now accept only boolean values

Content API `$null` and `$notNull` now accept only `true`, `t`, `1`, `false`, `f` and `0`, in any case. `FALSE` and `no` used to be read as `true`. `FALSE` now means false, and `no`, `yes`, `null`, an empty value or any other value returns 400. A bare `filters[price][$null]` still reads as false. In `strapi.db.query`, `{ $null: 'false' }` now means `IS NOT NULL` (it meant `IS NULL`), and unknown values throw `InvalidBooleanError`. MCP `list_*` tools now take only `true` or `false` for these operators.

([#28513](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28513))

#### TypeScript: component filters are now type-checked like content type filters

Unknown keys, password attributes and `documentId` in a component filter no longer compile. Inside a component, a relation, media or component attribute takes `{ id: 5 }` or one operator such as `{ $eq: 5 }`, not a bare `5`. Reading a component filter with a `string` key (`filters.seo?.[key]`) no longer compiles under `noImplicitAny`, so type the key as a union of the component's attribute names. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

([#28518](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28518))

#### Media `connect` and `disconnect` now change the field instead of replacing it

In the Content API, the Document Service and `strapi.db.query`, `{ connect: [] }`, `{ disconnect: [] }` and `{}` used to clear a media field. They now leave it unchanged, so to clear a field send `null` or `{ set: [] }`. `connect` on a single media field now replaces the file, and creating an entry with `{ connect: [id] }` now attaches it. A bare `{ set: null }` still clears a media field. The admin panel is not affected.

([#27116](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/27116))

#### A relation to a disabled plugin's content type now fails boot

An inverse-side (`mappedBy`) relation to a content type from a disabled or uninstalled plugin used to cause a `TypeError` at boot, or 500 errors later in the Content Manager and on publish. Boot now fails with `Metadata for "<uid>" not found`. Enable the plugin again, or remove the relation attribute from the content type's `schema.json`.

([#28542](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28542))

#### An inverse relation with no owner now fails boot

An inverse-side (`mappedBy`) relation that no owner points back to used to boot, but it stored nothing. Boot now fails with `mappedBy attribute <mappedBy> in <target> must be a relation to <uid> with inversedBy "<attribute>"`. Add `inversedBy: "<attribute>"` to the owner relation on the target, or remove the inverse attribute. There is no warning-only step first, so this can also hit third-party plugins.

([#28561](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28561))

#### Content-Type Builder services now reject `displayName: null` on edit

`editContentType`, and `updateSchema` with `action: 'update'`, used to keep the stored name when given `displayName: null`. They now throw "A content type requires a displayName". Omitting `displayName` still keeps the stored name. `generateAPI` and component creation also throw when the name is missing or empty. Only code that calls these services directly is affected, because the admin and the HTTP routes already rejected these values.

([#28598](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28598))

#### TypeScript: `editComponent` now takes the Content-Type Builder input shape

The `editComponent` payload is now typed as Content-Type Builder input, with `displayName`, `category` and `icon` at the top level. Passing a loaded `Struct.ComponentSchema` through `@strapi/content-type-builder/strapi-server` no longer compiles. That call already wrote a component with no `displayName`. `strapi.plugin('content-type-builder').service('components')` is unaffected.

([#28529](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/28529))

#### Editor and Author roles on existing projects still have no access to localized content

On a new database, the default Editor and Author roles now get the default locale on localized content types. Projects whose default roles already exist keep them as they are, with no locale and so no access to localized content. Select the locales in Settings > Roles to give these roles access. The boot warning about removed permissions now gives the reason for each removal.

### ⚠️ Potential Breaking Changes

**Improved typing of `@directus/env` to contain known env vars and added `milliseconds` and `bytes` cast types for human... ([#28282](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28282))**
Env vars are now cast more strictly:

- Booleans only accept `true`, `false`, `1` and `0` (case-insensitive). Other values (eg `yes`) are invalid, where some
  vars previously treated any non-empty value as enabled (eg `SERVE_APP=FALSE`)
- Plain number durations (eg `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL=900`) are read as milliseconds, use a unit to be explicit (eg `15m`)
- Invalid values log a warning and fall back to the default (or `false` for booleans without one)
- Variables without a value in a `.env` file (eg `KEY=`) are treated as not configured and fall back to the default. Use
  `KEY=""` for an empty value, eg `DB_PASSWORD=""` for a database user without a password, as `DB_PASSWORD=` is now
  reported as missing
- Empty values of string and list vars (eg `KEY=""` in a `.env` file or `KEY=` in the process environment) are kept as an
  empty string or list instead of falling back to the default, eg an empty `EMAIL_SENDMAIL_PATH` is no longer replaced by
  `/usr/sbin/sendmail`. Empty values of other vars still fall back to the default
- `useEnv` returns parsed values: durations and sizes are numbers, lists are arrays
- The `env` passed to API extensions is typed as `Record<string, unknown>` instead of `Record<string, any>`, so env vars
  need to be narrowed before use

**Bounded the work that parsing query parameters can cause ([#28521](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28521))**
`filter` and `deep` are now rejected with an `InvalidQueryError` once they exceed a limit on total node count or nesting depth.

The node allowance is spent across a whole query, so a filter nested under `deep` draws from what is left rather than starting over. Set a limit to `Infinity` to opt out of it.

- `QUERY_FILTER_MAX_NODES` (default `10000`) — total `filter`/`deep` nodes
- `QUERY_FILTER_MAX_DEPTH` (default `50`) — nesting depth of a filter or of `deep`
- `GRAPHQL_QUERY_SELECTION_LIMIT` (default `10000`) — fields a GraphQL operation may select across all its root fields once its fragments are expanded, checked during validation

`QUERY_FILTER_MAX_NODES` is the one most likely to be reached. Every object, array and value counts,
so `{"id":{"_in":[…]}}` costs one node per value plus three, and an `_in` of more than 9997 values is
rejected.

A `$NOW(...)` adjustment longer than 64 characters is now treated as unparseable, which also rejects
a zero-padded amount that long, such as `$NOW(0000…0005s)`. A dynamic variable path deeper than 25
segments now resolves to its default value.

A `$CURRENT_USER`, `$CURRENT_ROLE`, `$CURRENT_ROLES` or `$CURRENT_POLICIES` path in a query filter is
now held to `MAX_RELATIONAL_DEPTH`, the same as the fields it is fetched as, and is rejected with an
`InvalidQueryError` beyond it.

**Enforced `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` on incoming WebSocket messages ([#28521](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28521))**
A WebSocket message larger than `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` (default `1mb`) now closes the connection with
code `1009`. The setting applied only to REST bodies before this, leaving a message bounded by the
100MB `ws` allows on its own.

**Fixed websocket subscription delete events not enforcing read permissions ([#28522](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28522))**
WebSocket Subscription delete events now require read access to, at minimum, the `id` field and no item rules on the events collection. Users who don't meet these requirements will not receive delete events.

**Added proxy support via `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` environment variables ([#28057](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28057))**
- Requests now go through the proxy set in `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`. If these variables are already set and S3 should be reached directly, add the S3 host to `NO_PROXY`
- Proxy variables are read from the process environment, not from the Directus `.env` or config file
- `STORAGE_<LOCATION>_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT` (5 seconds by default) also covers the proxy handshake and may need raising for slow proxies

### A half-applied bump fails far from its cause

- **React is the one that breaks silently.** `@medusajs/ui`, `@medusajs/draft-order`, and `@medusajs/loyalty-plugin` declare `react` / `react-dom` `^19.3.1` as peer dependencies (`@medusajs/medusa` declares an optional `react-dom` `^19.3.1` peer), and `@medusajs/dashboard` depends on React 19 directly. If the project keeps React 18, or widens its range to `^18 || ^19`, the package manager installs **two copies of React**. Nothing errors at install or build time; admin widgets and routes then fail at runtime in the browser (typically the "Invalid hook call" class of error) far from the dependency that caused it. Pin the project to `^19.3.1` exactly as the notes say — a widened range is not supported.
- **Vite**: the admin bundler depends on `vite` `^8.3.8` itself. A project that lists `vite` (the official starters do) and keeps `^7` gets two copies.
- `tailwindcss` and `vite` reach the admin through `@medusajs/admin-sdk` / the admin bundler. A project that does not list them does not need to add them.

## 3. Express 5: custom API route and middleware matchers

Medusa now runs on Express 5 (`^5.3.0`, also the `express` peer range of `@medusajs/utils`), which matches routes with `path-to-regexp` 8. This affects `matcher` strings in `src/api/middlewares.ts` (and any plugin's), and code reading `req.params` / `req.body` in custom routes.

- **Bare `*` keeps working.** Medusa rewrites each bare `*` in a string matcher to a numbered optional wildcard: `/admin/products/*` becomes `/admin/products/{*splat0}`, a second `*` becomes `{*splat1}`, and so on. It matches the same paths as before. `RegExp` matchers pass through unchanged. The native Express 5 syntax is `{*splat}` (for example `/admin/products/{*splat}`).
- **Every other Express 4 string syntax now throws at startup**: regex groups (`/admin/(products|collections)`), optional params (`/:id?`), and `+`. ## Security Fixes

### Improved API access protection

Fixed an API access-control vulnerability that could expose protected data.
API responses and Store API searches now consistently respect field visibility restrictions.
Validation errors with code `FRAMEWORK__ACCESSOR_NOT_ALLOWED` now use HTTP status 400 instead of 500.
Entity aggregations in the Admin API and in app scripts now also require the read privilege of the aggregated entity.

Association visibility is checked against the API scope of the caller.
This applies to Admin API and Store API requests, as well as app scripts using `services.repository` or `services.store`.
In 6.7, associations in the `associations` parameter that are not visible in that scope are ignored, including their nested criteria.
Selections in the `fields` parameter that traverse a non-visible association are also ignored; valid selections and fields added by server code are preserved.
If no field selections remain, the normal read behavior applies, with API response visibility still enforced.
With debug mode enabled, these requests emit a deprecation notice identifying the ignored association or field selection.
Starting with 6.8, these requests fail with HTTP 400 and `FRAMEWORK__ACCESSOR_NOT_ALLOWED`; remove non-visible associations and field selections that traverse them from requests and app scripts before upgrading.
Filters, sorting and aggregations retain their existing validation.
App permissions do not grant additional access to protected associations through `services.store`.

### ExtensionAPI repository operations no longer expose Administration access tokens

Fixed an ExtensionAPI vulnerability that could expose the signed-in Administration user's access token to an app.
The `save`, `saveAll`, and `delete` repository operations no longer return raw HTTP responses.
Apps should await completion of these operations to detect success.

### Clone overwrites enforce field protection and association permissions

The Admin API clone action and `CloneBehavior` validate explicit root, nested association, translation and extension overwrites using the caller's field write protection and create/update permissions.
Association overwrites remain supported, including partial payloads and `null` values that suppress copying.
Copied source values retain their existing clone behavior without requiring additional association write privileges.
Creating the root clone still requires create permission; updating an existing associated entity requires its update permission, while creating a new associated entity requires its create permission.

### Recovery associations removed

Remove criteria using the `user.recoveryUser` or `customer.recoveryCustomer` associations, which were removed in a security update.
`UserEntity::getRecoveryUser()`, `UserEntity::setRecoveryUser()`, `CustomerEntity::getRecoveryCustomer()`, and `CustomerEntity::setRecoveryCustomer()` are deprecated and will be removed in 6.8.
The outgoing `user_recovery.user` and `customer_recovery.customer` associations remain available.

### Extension XML files are parsed without resolving document types

App manifests, plugin `config.xml` files, custom entity, admin UI, flow, CMS and custom field XML files are now read through `Shopware\Core\Framework\Util\XmlParser`.
It rejects any document type declaration before libxml can load an external DTD or entity.
Previously the DTD was resolved before the document type was rejected, so an administrator who may upload extensions could read local files through a crafted manifest (XML external entity injection).

Empty, missing or malformed extension XML files now fail with a `UtilException` (`UTIL__XML_PARSING_FAILED`, HTTP 400) instead of Symfony's `InvalidArgumentException`.
The error messages are unchanged.
The PHPStan rule `NoXmlUtilsParsingRule` in the core rule set reports direct calls to `XmlUtils::parse()` and `XmlUtils::loadFile()` outside tests.
Use `XmlParser` for XML that may come from an extension.
`XmlParser` is public API, so extensions that parse XML from an untrusted source should use it instead of `XmlUtils` as well.

### Twig templates only read the request context

Twig templates can no longer call methods that change the request context or the request, such as setters.
Reading them stays possible, for example `context.languageId`, and so does adding an extension with `addExtension()` or `addArrayExtension()`.
Such a call fails with the error code `FRAMEWORK__TWIG_METHOD_CALL_NOT_ALLOWED`; make the change in PHP instead, for example in an event subscriber.

### App Script services use a separate context for each call

The `repository` and `writer` App Script services now use their own context for every call.
Context changes made during one call no longer carry over to later calls.

### Aggregation identifiers and JSON paths reject comment and quote characters

Aggregation names and range aggregation keys containing a single or double quote, the `--`, `/*`, or `*/` SQL comment markers, a backslash, or a semicolon are now rejected with a `FRAMEWORK__INVALID_AGGREGATION_QUERY` (HTTP 400), in addition to the previously rejected backtick, question mark, colon, and control characters.
JSON field access paths used in filters, sortings, and aggregations now reject the `/*` and `*/` SQL comment markers and control characters.
From 6.8.0.0 this fails as a `FRAMEWORK__DBAL_INVALID_IDENTIFIER` (HTTP 400); on 6.7 the same input is rejected with an `InvalidArgumentException` (HTTP 500).
Either way the request is blocked and no data is returned.
These characters could desynchronise PDO placeholder parsing from the database server under emulated prepares on PHP 8.2 and 8.3 leading to SQL Injection.

# Spree 6.0.5

A patch release with marketplace, dashboard and search fixes. Sellers can now build variants from the marketplace's option types, resource tables sort by clicking a column header, and stores whose language differs from the application's get working search and product exports again. The dashboard can now report its errors to Sentry, and the CLI keeps new projects' docs and agent skills matched to their Spree version.

```bash
npx spree upgrade
```

---

## ✨ New features

- **Variants from the marketplace's option types.** Sellers can now pick the marketplace's option types and values, such as size and colour, to build variants in the seller panel, and a product type offers its option types on a new listing. Adding new option types or values stays with the marketplace, and the Seller API and seller imports now refuse values the store does not have. [#15219](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15219)
- **Error tracking for the dashboard and seller panel.** The new `@spree/dashboard-sentry` package sends admin dashboard and seller panel errors to Sentry with one `initDashboardSentry({ dsn })` call. The seller panel now shows the same error screen with a retry button as the admin dashboard. [#15220](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15220)
- **Store logo and social accounts in the Store API.** The current store now returns its logo, meta keywords, Facebook, X and Instagram accounts and customer support email, so a storefront can read them from the API instead of environment variables. [#15216](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15216)

## 🧭 Admin dashboard improvements

- **Sort by clicking a column header.** Resource tables sort by a sortable column when you click its header; a second click flips the direction, and the header shows the current one. [#15230](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15230)
- **Store logo, meta keywords and social media in Store settings.** Store settings gains a logo upload, a meta keywords field in the search engine listing and a Social media card for Facebook, X and Instagram. [#15216](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15216)

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- The products list's SKU column shows each product's SKU again instead of "—". [#15218](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15218)
- Search results and product CSV exports include product names and descriptions for a store whose language differs from the application's default. [#15226](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15226)
- Product updates, imports and sample data no longer overload Meilisearch with "Too Many Requests" errors, so the search index keeps up with every change. [#15207](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15207), [#15224](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15224)
- The Store API cart accepts the extra cart attributes an extension registers. [#15210](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15210)
- OAuth apps that redirect to `http://localhost` are authorized on any port, as they already were on `127.0.0.1`. [#15212](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15212)

## 🛠 Developer experience

- `spree_core` now requires Doorkeeper `~> 6.0.0.rc3`. Doorkeeper rc3 refuses out-of-band redirect URIs (`urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob`), so an OAuth app registered with one stops authorizing; give it a real redirect URI. [#15212](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15212)
- Calling a Ruby API that Spree 6.0 removed now names its replacement and links the upgrade guide in the error. The full list is in [Removed APIs](https://spreecommerce.org/docs/developer/upgrades/removed-apis). [#15197](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15197)
- Deprecated Ruby APIs now keep working until 6.3, and deprecated Store API fields, request names and webhook event names until 6.5, instead of being removed in 6.1. [#15221](https://github.com/spree/spree/pull/15221)

### Patch Changes

- e9fd841: Update the `@verdaccio/*` modules to the `next-9` npm dist-tag.
  
  **Patch changes**
  
  - `@verdaccio/middleware`: Fix requests returning 404 when Verdaccio's Express application is mounted under ([#6483](https://github.com/verdaccio/verdaccio/pull/6483))
    a path such as `/registry`. The request logger now preserves the path Express
    uses to route requests while continuing to log the complete original URL. This
    restores web package listing, search, login, and registry API requests under the
    mount path, including when middleware plugins continue asynchronously.
  
    The default suppression of static-file and successful ping logs also works under
    the mount path; failed pings remain visible. No configuration changes are needed.
    The problem was reproduced on the 9.x development line at
    `9.0.0-next-9.45`. The separate asynchronous web-routing failure reported in
    Verdaccio 6.x requires the fixes for that release line.
  - `@verdaccio/ui-theme`: Fix the web UI failing to load parts of itself when Verdaccio is served under `url_prefix`. ([#6480](https://github.com/verdaccio/verdaccio/pull/6480))
  
    The UI loads some of its files on demand, such as the code and styles of the package detail page. Those requests went to `/-/static/` at the root of the host instead of below `url_prefix`, so behind a reverse proxy that only forwards the prefix they failed with 404. Package pages then showed "Something went wrong", and other pages could lose styles. The UI now requests these files relative to its own location, so they follow `url_prefix`. Registries served at the root of a host behave as before.
  
    This affected `@verdaccio/ui-theme` 9.0.0-next-9.2 and later, the web UI Verdaccio 6 and 7 ship. A reverse proxy rule that forwards `/-/static/` at the root to Verdaccio as a workaround is no longer needed.
  
    No configuration change is needed.
  - `@verdaccio/proxy`, `@verdaccio/store`: Fix the `X-Forwarded-For` header sent to uplinks. ([#6476](https://github.com/verdaccio/verdaccio/pull/6476))
  
    Tarball requests to an uplink carried the literal value `undefined`, because no client address is passed on that path. A reverse proxy or firewall in front of the uplink could log, rate limit or reject those requests under a bogus address. The header is now only generated when the client address is known, so tarball requests carry no `X-Forwarded-For`, as in 6.x.
  
    Metadata requests forward the `X-Forwarded-For` chain the client request arrived with, followed by the client address. Since 7.x they sent the client address alone and dropped the incoming chain that 6.x forwarded.
  
    An `X-Forwarded-For` value set in the `headers` option of an uplink takes precedence however the header name is capitalised. A lower-case `x-forwarded-for` lost against the generated value on tarball requests.
  
    When the uplink goes through `http_proxy` or `https_proxy` no client-origin header is generated, as before; a value set in the uplink `headers` is still sent.
  
    No configuration change is needed.

## [1.186.0](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep/releases/tag/v1.186.0) - 2026-11-17

### ### Added

- Secrets findings can include a versioned `secret_hash` when requested (e.g., with `--compute-secret-hash`). This hash comprises the secret value and values used in the validators, to allow for identification of the same secret being present at multiple locations (cf. `match_based_id`, which depends on the location of the finding). (SCRT-987)

### ### Changed

- Semgrep's release binaries are now built with cross-module inlining enabled, so scans use about 5-11% less CPU time. (release-profile)

### ### Fixed

- pro: Rules with `interfile: true` now keep Pro intrafile interprocedural taint analysis when scanning languages without interfile support (e.g. OCaml, Rust), so taint through helper functions in the same file is reported. (interfile-rule-intrafile-fallback)
- `semgrep mcp` now respects `SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS=off`, which turns off its
  metrics and tracing like `SEMGREP_MCP_DISABLE_TRACING=true`. Its metrics and
  logs also no longer include scan error messages, semgrep's stderr, or
  supply chain scan results. (mcp-telemetry-redact)
- Pro: Python type filters now recognize calls to builtin classes and builtin functions when using interfile analysis or single-file type resolution. (CODE-10241)
- Dependency resolution errors for pip and setup.py projects now include the failing command's error output (for example `No module named 'setuptools'`) instead of an empty message. setup.py projects now resolve when `python3` is Python 3.12 or later, whose virtual environments no longer include setuptools. (SC-4349)
- Python CLI usage metrics will now be sent to the URL set by SEMGREP_METRICS_URL. The default destination remains unchanged. (SMS-3925)

### ### Infra/Release Changes

- Updated tree-sitter-requirements grammar to v0.5.0 (no behavior change). (requirements-v0.5.0)

### Breaking Changes

- The C/C++ extractor no longer supports Brotli compression. Users invoking the extractor directly should replace `--trap-compression=brotli` or `--tar-entry-compression=brotli` with the corresponding `zstd` option. The `--brotli-quality` option has also been removed.

### Security Fixes

- When invoked by `codeql test run`, extractors for XML, YAML, and Java `.properties` files run in a
  mode that traverses the source root directory and extracts all relevant files. This mode has been
  updated so that it no longer follows symbolic links.

### Bug Fixes

- When choosing the default queries for a language whose extractor is found on `--search-path`, the CLI now uses the extractor's `default_queries` property instead of `codeql/<language>-queries`.
- `codeql test run` now accepts `.qlref` consistency queries passed via `--consistency-queries` as it already does for ordinary unit tests, and applies the same `.qlref` precedence: if a `.ql` file has a synonymous `.qlref` file, the `.qlref` file is resolved and run instead, and the `.ql` file is skipped.

### Query Language Changes

- The `string` type now has built-in member predicates `startsWith(string prefix)`,
  `endsWith(string suffix)`, and `contains(string substring)`. These perform
  case-sensitive matching of literal strings, without wildcards or regular
  expressions. All three predicates hold for an empty argument.

> [!IMPORTANT] > ## Upgrading Docker Compose from 26.0? Read the migration guide first > **Do not start 26.1 with the 26.0.7 storage settings left in place.** Storage variables move into `x-storage`, `minio` and `s3` are no longer valid types, and in `multi` mode 26.1 does not read the old per-project buckets. Attachments, avatars, plugins, and the integration salt become unreachable. > > - **[Migration from ReportPortal 26.0 to 26.1](https://github.com/reportportal/reportportal/wiki/Migration-v26.1)** covers filesystem storage, S3-compatible storage, and Amazon S3. ## 1. Breaking changes: **1. Roles and permissions model** Project roles **Project Manager**, **Member**, **Customer**, and **Operator** are replaced by a three-level access model: **Instance → Organization → Project**. | Level | Roles / permissions | | ----- | ------------------- | | Instance | **Administrator**, **Regular user** | | Organization | **Manager**, **Member** | | Project | **Editor**, **Viewer** | Automatic migration mapping: | Before 26.1 | After 26.1 | | ----------- | ---------- | | Project Manager / Member / Customer | Organization **Member** + project **Editor** | | Operator | Organization **Member** + project **Viewer** | Migration can **increase or reduce** project access. Before upgrade: identify users who should not become Editors, Operators who still need Editor rights, and who should get organization **Manager**. After upgrade: review organization roles and project permissions. **2. Organizations as a required structural level** - **Launches retention policy** — configured at organization level as a **ceiling**; projects can be stricter, not looser - **Email server integration** — can be configured at organization level and reused by projects Other integrations and **notification rules** remain at **project** level in this release. Open-source instances keep one default organization; multiple organizations are a premium capability. **3. Authentication packaging** **SSO** and **LDAP** are **Enterprise** features in 26.1. **Built-in** and **GitHub** authentication remain part of the **open-source** edition. **4. Users now sign in with email** Login uses the user **email** (instead of the previous username-based login where applicable). Update bookmarks, SSO mappings, and any automation that authenticates with a username. **5. Platform / deployment** - **Java 25** runtime for backend services (was Java 21). - **service-authorization** is merged into **service-api** (single API process; update compose/Helm accordingly). - File storage moves from **Jclouds** to **Apache OpenDAL** (filesystem / S3). Validate attachments, avatars, and plugin upload after upgrade. - Database structure rework and related migrations (including attributes / auth integration migration). Plan downtime and backup. - RabbitMQ declarations updated for **RabbitMQ 4.3+** compatibility. - Custom / third-party **plugins** must be rebuilt against the 26.1 Plugin API (Organizations-aware endpoints, project key usage where applicable). **6. API clients and integrations** Clients, reporters, and automation should use the Organizations-era API surface (organization-scoped resources, **project key** where previously only project name was used). For **existing projects**, nothing changes after migration: the current identifier keeps working, and users do not need to update integrations. For **new projects**, use the **project key**. Review plugin command endpoints (e.g. Test Executions) if you call them directly. **7. Docker Compose** Details and step-by-step procedures are in the [migration guide](https://github.com/reportportal/reportportal/blob/26.1/MIGRATION-DOCKER-26.1.md). - **Storage settings moved to `x-storage`.** In 26.0.7, `DATASTORE_*` lived in `x-environment` (API, Jobs, UAT) and again in `x-analyzer-environment`. 26.1 reads them from `x-storage` only. A value left in the old block is not applied. - **`DATASTORE_TYPE: minio` and `s3` are no longer valid.** Use `s3-compatible` (MinIO, SeaweedFS, Ceph RGW, and other S3 APIs) or `aws-s3`. `filesystem` is unchanged. The 26.0.7 example spelling `DATASTORE_SECRETSKEY` must be `DATASTORE_SECRETKEY`, or the secret is ignored. - **The `multi` object layout changed.** 26.0 used one bucket per project (`prj-`). 26.1 keeps those names as folders in the default bucket (`rp-bucket/prj-/`), so existing objects must be copied. Filesystem storage and `RP_FEATURE_FLAGS: singleBucket` need no copy. Docker Compose does not copy objects and does not rewrite paths in PostgreSQL. - **`DATASTORE_PATH` is for API and Jobs only** (`/data/storage`). The analyzer ignores it. Filesystem models stay at `FILESYSTEM_DEFAULT_PATH` (`/data/storage/analyzer`). `ANALYZER_BINARYSTORE_TYPE` is deprecated in service-auto-analyzer 6.0.0: remove it. The analyzer reads `DATASTORE_TYPE` and logs a warning if the old variable is still set. - **The commented MinIO secret default is now `rppassword`** (was `miniopassword`). A value set in `STORAGE_SECRETKEY` still wins. Write the password you use today into `DATASTORE_SECRETKEY`. - **`service-authorization` (UAT) and `service-index` are removed.** Start with `docker compose up -d --remove-orphans`. The token endpoint moves from `/uat/sso/oauth/token` to `/api/sso/oauth/token`. - **The built-in `superadmin` login becomes `admin@reportportal.internal`.** ## 2. What's new: **1. Organizations** A new level above projects for portfolio-scale administration: - All Organizations view; drill-down into organization projects - Organization Managers see all org projects; Members see only assigned projects - Create projects and manage user assignments (org role + Editor/Viewer) in one place - Organization

**This release fixes a security vulnerability ([GHSA-v887-64wg-qqc9](https://github.com/axllent/mailpit/security/advisories/GHSA-v887-64wg-qqc9)): a specially crafted message could crash Mailpit's SMTP server. Updating is recommended.**

It also includes a large number of smaller fixes and hardening changes from a review of the codebase. Almost all of them are under the hood: tighter limits on memory and CPU use, more careful parsing of messages and headers, and better handling of edge cases. For most users nothing should look or behave differently.

### A few changes may need attention when upgrading:

- Flags and environment variables that have been deprecated for over two years have been removed. A relay config that still uses `recipient-allowlist` will now stop Mailpit from starting: rename it to `allowed-recipients`.
- Some settings are now checked at startup and refused if invalid, where they were previously ignored or treated as 0: relay and forward ports, `return-path`, `--max-age`, integer environment variables, and empty authentication credentials.
- The send API returns new responses: 400 for a From address that cannot be parsed, 413 for a message over the maximum message size, and 503 (with `Retry-After`) when too many messages are being sent at once.
- Messages are limited to 100 tags.

### Chore
- Reduce CPU cost of message ingestion ([#771](https://github.com/axllent/mailpit/issues/771))
- Recover from panics in SMTP sessions
- Use the SpamAssassin server's required score to decide what is spam
- Limit the HTML parsing of the embedded message view
- Refuse to render HTML over 10 MiB in the message view
- Limit how many bytes of messages are stored at once
- Treat a bare CR in headers as text, as Go and Postfix do
- Stop the storage background goroutines before re-initialising
- Limit the terms of a search and the memory a search holds
- Cache host names of SMTP clients for a short time
- Lower the size limit of proxied images and fonts to 10 MiB
- Limit the size of the messages a websocket client can send
- Remove deprecated flags and environment settings
- Validate relay and forward ports and return-path at startup
- Update Go dependencies
- Update node dependencies
- Update Github Actions dependencies

### Fix
- Make field searches case-insensitive for non-ASCII characters
- Show the current UTC offset in the timezone setting ([#773](https://github.com/axllent/mailpit/issues/773))
- Make dump paging and failure handling fail closed
- Make credential loading and matching fail closed
- Harden the HTML checker against slow and concurrent input
- Bound and clean up link checking
- Stop log messages injecting terminal control sequences
- Silence the logger once for the POP3 tests
- Correct POP3 TOP and dot-stuffing, and harden connection handling
- Make the database last-action time safe for concurrent use
- Limit the number of tags on a message to 100
- Bound the Prometheus tag series and harden the metrics server
- Harden the Rspamd integration
- Harden the snakeoil self-signed certificate generator
- Harden the SpamAssassin integration
- Reuse webhook connections to prevent dropped webhooks under load ([#772](https://github.com/axllent/mailpit/issues/772))
- Prevent SMTP crash on unparseable media type with RFC 2231 parameter ([GHSA-v887-64wg-qqc9](https://github.com/axllent/mailpit/security/advisories/GHSA-v887-64wg-qqc9))
- Stop the version lookup blocking requests and fix its backoff
- Stop EXIF rotation copying large images and limit thumbnail decodes
- Limit the size of progressive JPEGs that are thumbnailed
- Remove List-Unsubscribe comments in a single pass and limit its length
- Locate message headers by position when rewriting them
- Use the text part for the snippet when the HTML has no text
- Keep text that is the same as a skipped element's name
- Trim truncated tags and stop PrepareSocket removing files
- Make --smtp-strict-rfc-headers cover all non-CRLF header line breaks
- Reduce the cost of HTML redirect stripping and text snippets
- Set the start time when the stats package loads
- Stream the message to Postmark without copying it
- Stop thumbnails for requests whose client has gone
- Reject messages with unreadable headers permanently
- Send only CRLF line breaks when relaying, and keep the stored body
- Remove whitespace before the colon of header names
- Handle more IDs than SQLite has placeholders for
- Tell the web UI about every message a search deleted
- Do not fail searches for sizes beyond what a database can compare
- Look up the client's host name without holding up other connections
- Time out TLS clients who never start the handshake
- Limit how much memory messages being received can use
- Make SMTP Shutdown wait for the open sessions
- Give relaying and forwarding time limits
- End the transaction when a MAIL command is refused
- Close the connections the proxy opens to fetch assets
- Allow sending messages through the API over a Unix socket
- Limit the cost of proxying a stylesheet
- Limit and cache the SpamAssassin checks of messages
- Make the Chaos settings and the HTML preview route safe for concurrent use
- Release a message to the addresses which were checked
- Rewrite the inline image links of a message in a single pass
- Limit the memory used by messages sent through the API
- Reject invalid integer environment variables instead of using 0
- Use the default sender when ingesting messages without a From address
- Reject --max-age values too large to calculate the prune cutoff
- Apply the return-path option to forwarded and auto-relayed messages
- Keep the quotes of an address in the sender and recipients which are sent
- Give the sendmail command and ingest time limits when sending
- Send the messages of the sendmail command with CR LF line breaks
- Reject line breaks in the From address of the send API
- Resolve proxied CSS assets after redirect

RabbitMQ `4.4.1` is a maintenance release in the `4.4.x` [release series](https://www.rabbitmq.com/release-information).

It is **strongly recommended** that you read [4.4.0 release notes](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/releases/tag/v4.4.0)
in detail if upgrading from a version prior to `4.4.0`.

### Minimum Supported Erlang Version

The minimum supported Erlang version for this release series is `27.0`.

[RabbitMQ and Erlang/OTP Compatibility Matrix](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/which-erlang) has more details on Erlang version requirements for RabbitMQ.

Nodes **will fail to start** on older Erlang releases.


## Changes Worth Mentioning

Release notes can be found on GitHub at [rabbitmq-server/release-notes](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/tree/v4.4.x/release-notes).

### Core Server

#### Bug Fixes

 * Definition import on boot could hang on Erlang 28 because of a missing dependency
   between boot steps.

   GitHub issues: [#17914](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/17914), [#17915](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17915)

 * Virtual host records written by older versions could have their limits set to `undefined`,
   which made definition export fail.

   GitHub issue: [#18137](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18137)

 * Definition export no longer includes bindings to exclusive queues, and definition import
   skips bindings to `amq.*` queues with a warning instead of failing.

   GitHub issue: [#17838](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17838)

 * Definition export no longer includes bindings of queues that were concurrently deleted,
   and definition import skips bindings of missing server-named queues.

   GitHub issue: [#17841](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17841)

 * A quorum queue leader health check could report a queue with a leader as unhealthy, for example
   after a leadership change or when the node running the check did not host a replica.

   GitHub issue: [#18274](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18274)

 * When a new quorum queue member is started, the lowest `ra` machine version among the
   reachable members is now used.

   GitHub issues: [#18053](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/18053), [#18055](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18055)

 * The quorum queue message expiration timer is now capped at one year.

   GitHub issue: [#17815](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17815)

 * The metadata store now waits for Raft members with a capped timeout, which avoids an endless
   retry loop in some operational scenarios.

   GitHub issues: [#18114](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/18114), [#18233](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18233)

 * Classic queue CRC32 checksums are now calculated in a way that is compatible with future Erlang releases.

   GitHub issues: [#18161](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/18161), [#18216](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18216)

 * Classic queues: a crash report for a deleted queue now shows the original error.

   GitHub issue: [#18208](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18208)

 * Message conversion between AMQP 0-9-1 and AMQP 1.0 no longer fails on `decimal`
   and `null` header values, nor on `float`, `double` and `null` annotation values
   set by the AMQP 1.0 `modified` outcome.

   GitHub issues: [#18042](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18042), [#18156](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18156)

 * Hourly log file rotation (for example, `log.file.rotation.date = $H30`) never rotated the file.

   GitHub issues: [#7562](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/7562), [#18263](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18263)

 * Streams now handle non-string `x-stream-filter-value` values gracefully.

   GitHub issue: [#18147](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18147)

 * AMQP 0-9-1 header and argument tables are validated more strictly.

   GitHub issues: [#18213](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18213), [#18243](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18243)

 * AMQP 1.0 frames are validated more strictly.

   GitHub issues: [#17954](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17954), [#18029](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18029)

 * AMQP 1.0 SQL filter expressions are evaluated more defensively.

   GitHub issue: [#18302](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18302)

 * An AMQP 1.0 session no longer crashes when its writer process has already exited
   during connection closure.

   GitHub issue: [#18070](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18070)

 * Credential expiry handling improvements.

   GitHub issues: [#17857](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17857), [#17979](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17979), [#17980](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17980)

 * [Proxy Protocol](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/networking#proxy-protocol) handling improvements.

   GitHub issue: [#17995](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17995)

 * Dead lettering validates its targets more strictly.

   GitHub issue: [#18195](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18195)

 * Channels now send `channel.close-ok` with a short socket write timeout.

   GitHub issue: [#18242](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18242)

#### Enhancements

 * AMQP 0-9-1 channels now use flow control when sending to the connection's socket writer process.

   GitHub issue: [#18049](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18049)

 * Closing a non-AMQP 0-9-1 connection (for example, an MQTT, STOMP, stream or AMQP 1.0 connection)
   is now cheaper on nodes with many tracked channels.

## Inkling 2 Mini
[Inkling 2 Mini](https://ollama.com/library/inkling-2-mini) from Thinking Machines is a 26B parameter model with 5.4B active.

Its looped layers give it more computation per token than its size suggests, and it still fits on a Mac at about 20GB. It handles text and images, tool calls, and thinking, and scores 79.2% on SWE-Bench Verified).

```
  ollama run inkling-2-mini
```

Note: inkling-2-mini is supported on Apple silicon only in this release.  PC support will follow in an upcoming release.

 ## What's Changed
- `ollama launch claude` supports Claude Code's deferred tool loading, so MCP tools are loaded when needed instead of all at
once
- Ollama on Apple silicon now serves multiple requests at once.
- `ollama launch opencode` sets thinking options from the model's metadata
- `ollama launch pi` refreshes Pi's model list after sign-in and passes along prompt arguments
- `ollama launch chatgpt --restore` asks before switching an active profile and preserves existing settings and chat history;
 quitting ChatGPT yourself now lets it exit through its own quit prompt
- Running `ollama` with no arguments in a non-interactive shell prints help instead of erroring
- Ctrl+C or Ctrl+G while in a multiline `"""` block leaves multiline mode instead of swallowing the next line
- Changing the context shift setting no longer reloads the model
- Vulkan now uses mmap for integrated GPUs, fixing `Failed to allocate pinned memory` load failures on shared-memory GPUs
- On Windows iGPUs, partially offloaded models no longer fail to allocate the KV cache
- Tool definitions passed through the API keep JSON schema keywords Ollama doesn't model instead of dropping them
- Disabling thinking now maps to the model's lowest supported reasoning level rather than being ignored
- Source builds can use prebuilt MLX-C and XGrammar binaries

    **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.16...v0.40.17-rc3

### Added

- **Bring your own computer with Tether.** Tether turns your own computer into part of Open WebUI: models from Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible server, OpenAPI and MCP tool servers and Open Terminal servers that you add in the Tether app now show up just for you in the model selector, the Tools list of the + menu and the terminal menu of any Open WebUI you connect, from whatever device you open it on, and Open WebUI reaches them through Tether, so their addresses, commands and keys never leave your computer. This needs Tether 0.1.14 or later, or 0.1.16 for MCP servers, tool servers and terminals need "ENABLE_TOOL_SERVERS" turned on, and a Tether model whose ID matches a model already in Open WebUI stays hidden. Tether replaces Direct Connections. [#34397](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34397)
- **Sandboxed agents on your own computer.** Tether 0.1.13 or later can lock the terminal on your computer into a sandbox, so models and coding agents work in your real files without reaching the rest of your machine: on macOS and supported Windows devices, Open Terminal and everything it launches, coding agents included, can only touch the one folder you pick, run offline unless you turn on Network access and accept no incoming connections, with no Docker, virtual machine or administrator setup needed. If the sandbox cannot be enforced, the terminal stays stopped instead of quietly running without it, and browser and desktop control stay off while it is on. Turn it on in Tether under Settings > Open Terminal > Sandbox.
- **Local MCP servers through Tether.** Open WebUI can now use MCP servers that run as a local command over stdio, the way many MCP servers are distributed, by launching them on your computer through Tether 0.1.16 or later, with no proxy such as mcpo and no port to open. Add one in Tether under Settings > Integrations > Tools with its command, or connect an MCP server by its web address, and pick it from the Tools list of the + menu. Local commands run with your own account's access, outside Tether's workspace sandbox.
- **A computer for every user.** With Terminals 0.4.0 or later connected, Open WebUI now hands out sandboxed computers on demand: anyone with Write access to the connection can create a terminal right from the terminal menu of the message input, pick whether everyone shares one machine or each user, chat or model gets its own, and set its image, CPU, memory, storage, network profile, environment variables, start directory and a setup script that, for example, clones a repository and installs its dependencies, without an administrator setting up each one. Terminals can be shared with users and groups and their instances started, stopped, restarted or deleted, a View files option opens any terminal's files without selecting it for the chat, System info shows how the setup script went, and those who manage a terminal can open the files and system info of other people's running instances. Start and Stop need Terminals 0.4.1 or later, the start directory and setup script need Open Terminal 0.17.7 or later in the terminal's image, and network profiles are the ones an administrator defined with "TERMINALS_NETWORK_PROFILES".
- **Coding agents as chat models.** Coding agents now work much like any other model in the chat. Hermes, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Goose and Qwen Code join Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Cline, Gemini CLI and Pi, and any other ACP agent added to Open Terminal with "OPEN_TERMINAL_ACP_AGENTS" works as well, once it is installed and signed in on the terminal. Auto for tool permissions now lets Codex, Claude Code and Grok approve routine actions themselves and pass on only what they escalate, and the reasoning effort in the advanced parameters now also applies to Claude Code, Pi and ACP agents that offer effort levels, such as OpenCode, which stop with an error when the chosen level is not offered for the model. Replies can now be regenerated and earlier messages edited, and a forked or cloned agent chat picks up where the original left off: Codex continues its own conversation from that point, other agents start over from the chat so far, and file changes the agent already made stay. Claude Code continues its own conversation too with the next Open Terminal release after 0.17.20 and until then asks you to update Open Terminal instead. The new agents and Auto for Claude Code and Grok need Open Terminal 0.17.19 or later, and effort for Claude Code, Pi and ACP agents needs 0.17.9 or later. [#34167](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/34167)
- **Pages open as tabs.** Notes, channels, the workspace, automations, the calendar, the playground, the home page and new chats from pinned models now open as tabs beside the current chat when you click or drag them from the sidebar, pick them in the user menu or follow a link to one of them in a chat message, and starting a new chat, also from a sidebar folder, keeps the open tabs.
- **Queued messages steer replies.** A message you send to your own chat while a reply is still running now waits on the server, so it is kept when you leave the page, and the reply wraps up at its next step so your message is answered right away with what it has done so far.
- **Instant first message.** The first message of a new chat now shows up right away while the chat is still being created, instead of only once it exists, unless files are still being uploaded with it.
- **Full chat in side chats.** Side chats now run the same chat as the main view, so message buttons, sources, token usage, follow-up suggestions, slash commands, queued messages, chat variables, web search settings, tool events such as code execution and input requests, HTML and SVG previews, notifications while the window is in the background, unsent text after a page reload and answers from several models at once now work there too, and a side chat's tab now has the chat menu.
